AccessReadDto.description: One tenant's access for one setting.

effective.description: The strictest access on the tenant's chain.

etag.description:
The tag a mutation of this pair must present: the stored row's, or the
absent-state tag. Also sent as the `ETag` header.

oneOf.description: The pair's own row, when one exists.

tenant_id.description: The tenant asked about.

AccountInfoDto.description: A chart-of-accounts entry in a response: coordinate + persistent `account_id`.

id.description:
GitHub's numeric user id, when the mirror stored one — a login can be
renamed and later reused, the id cannot.

type.description: `User`, `Bot` or `Organization`, under GitHub's own field name.

AggregationBucketDto.description:
Wire projection of [`usage_collector_sdk::AggregationBucket`]. `value`
is an arbitrary-precision `bigdecimal::BigDecimal` carried as a JSON
string via `usage_collector_sdk::serde_helpers::bigdecimal_str_option`
(the same string-on-the-wire discipline as `UsageRecord.value`, but
without `Decimal`'s magnitude ceiling); `None` materializes as `null`
per the SDK contract for empty-set buckets.

AggregationDimensionDto.description:
Wire projection of [`usage_collector_sdk::AggregationDimension`]. The
closed dimensions are encoded as snake-case bare strings; the
`metadata` form carries the declared key inline as
`{"metadata": "<key>"}` to mirror the SDK's `Metadata(MetadataKey)`
variant under the same lowercased external tag. (The macro-applied
`rename_all = "snake_case"` matches the SDK encoding here.)

AggregationOpDto.description:
Wire projection of [`usage_collector_sdk::AggregationOp`]. Identical
lowercase encoding — the wrapper exists so the OAS can pin the closed
enum schema without pulling `utoipa` into the SDK. (The macro-applied
`rename_all = "snake_case"` collapses to the same single-token form
as the SDK's `rename_all = "lowercase"` for these variants.)

AggregationResultDto.description:
Aggregated-query response body. Mirrors
[`usage_collector_sdk::AggregationResult`] — buckets are emitted in
plugin-defined order and a no-grouping query yields a single bucket
with an empty `key`.

AgingBucketDto.description:
One aged AR grain in the `GET /balances/ar-aging` response: the outstanding
receivable for a `(payer, currency, bucket)`.

AllocatePaymentRequest.description:
The `POST /payments/{payment_id}/allocations` request body: allocate a
settled payment's unallocated pool to the payer's open receivables (the
**money-out** side). The `payment_id` comes from the PATH (not the body —
see [`SettlePaymentRequest::into`] vs [`AllocatePaymentRequest::into_sdk`]),
so the lowering to the SDK type takes it as a parameter. `allocation_id` is
the idempotency key. `scale` is advisory.

When `splits` is omitted the `lump_minor` is applied by the tenant's
precedence policy and `hint_invoice_id` jumps one invoice to the front of
that fill order. When `splits` is supplied (Mode B), the precedence decision
is skipped and those explicit shares are validated against the open
receivables instead (each must name an open invoice and not over-allocate it;
the shares must sum to at most `lump_minor`) — a bad split is rejected
`ALLOCATION_SPLIT_INVALID`.

allocation_id.description: Idempotency key for the allocation (a re-issue replays).

hint_invoice_id.description:
Optional invoice to jump to the front of the oldest-first fill order.
Ignored when `splits` is supplied (Mode B bypasses the fill order).

lump_minor.description: The lump to apply in minor units, drained oldest-first across open AR.

scale.description: Advisory currency scale; the ledger resolves the authoritative one.

splits.description:
Optional caller-computed per-invoice split (Mode B escape hatch). `None`
⇒ the precedence policy decides the split.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this allocates within; the PEP gate
target. Carried in the body, not the path.

AllocatePaymentResponse.description:
The `POST /payments/{payment_id}/allocations` response: the posting handle
plus the per-invoice splits the allocation applied (always `201`).

AllocationDto.description:
One recorded allocation split in a response: how much of a payment was
applied to `invoice_id`, when, under which precedence policy. A row of
[`AllocatePaymentResponse::allocations`] and of the `GET
/payments/{payment_id}/allocations` list.

AllocationQueuedResponse.description:
The `POST /payments/{payment_id}/allocations` response when the payment is not
yet settled: the allocation was durably QUEUED for a later drain (HTTP 202
Accepted), not posted. `status` is the fixed `allocation-queued` token; `flow`
+ `business_id` are the queue key and `queued_at` the intake instant. No
posting handle / splits — nothing has posted yet (those arrive on the drain).
Mirrors the credit/settle status-varying rendering, but as a distinct body
shape since there is no `PostingRef` to surface.

business_id.description: The queue/dedup business id — the allocation's `allocation_id`.

queued_at.description: When the intake durably enqueued the request.

status.description: Always `allocation-queued` (a normal-body kebab-case token, not an error).

AllocationSplitDto.description:
One caller-computed allocation share (Mode B, §4.4 F-5): apply `amount_minor`
of the lump to `invoice_id`. A row of [`AllocatePaymentRequest::splits`].

ApprovalCommentDto.description: One comment / decision-reason on an approval's thread.

ApprovalDto.description: A dual-control approval rendered for the queue / detail views.

ArAgingDto.description: The `GET /balances/ar-aging` response: the open AR aged into buckets.

AttachmentDetailDto.description: Full attachment details returned by the GET attachment endpoint.

AttachmentSummaryDto.description: Lightweight attachment metadata embedded in Message responses.

AuditEntryDto.description:
The who/when/source/correlation dims of one posted entry, the
`GET …/audit/journal-entries/{entryId}` response (and one row of a document
history). A pure audit projection of `journal_entry`; carries no lines.

AuditPackExportDto.description:
Audit-pack export resource (Slice 6 §5/§10). `POST …/audit/packs` returns
this at `202 Accepted` (without `csv` — a job summary) with a `Location` to
`GET …/audit/packs/{exportId}`, which returns it again with `csv` populated
once `status = succeeded`.

csv.description:
The materialized CSV document; present once `status = succeeded` (omitted
from the `202` create response — poll the `Location`).

row_count.description: Data-row count of the CSV (excludes the header row).

target_tenant_id.description:
The tenant whose ledger was exported (= the caller's own on a routine
export).

AuditPackRequestDto.description:
`POST …/audit/packs` request body: the inquiry filter, an optional
cross-tenant `target_scope` (the tenant to open — a different tenant triggers
the forensic elevation gate), and the machine `reason_code` (the free-text
reason is the `X-Investigation-Reason` header). A cross-tenant pack needs
both a reason header and a `reason_code`.

reason_code.description:
Machine-readable investigation reason code (required for a cross-tenant
pack).

target_scope.description:
The tenant to open (defaults to the caller's own; a different tenant
triggers the forensic cross-tenant elevation gate).

AuditRecordDto.description:
One audit record, as `GET /settings-service/v1/settings/{key}/history`
returns it.

actor.description: Who did it, masked when the identity is PII the caller may not see.

change_set_id.description: The change set the mutation was produced under.

pre_value.description: The value before, as recorded; a secret was recorded masked.

request_id.description: The request that produced the record.

tenant_id.description:
The scope the record is about, or `null` for a record about the
setting's definition — the declaration created, changed, retired —
which belongs to no tenant and appears in every scope's history.

values_masked.description: Whether the recorded values were masked for this caller.

AuthenticatedUserDto.description:
GitHub-shaped `GET /user`. The mirror has no authenticated GitHub user
of its own, so it answers as itself: enough for a client to accept the
connection and show who it is talking to.

AuthzBarrierMode.description:
Controls how barriers (self-managed tenants) are handled during `AuthZ` evaluation.

Consistent with `tenant_resolver_sdk::BarrierMode`.

BalanceDto.description:
A read-back account-balance row in the `GET /balances` response. Carries both
the transaction-currency `balance_minor` and the Slice-5 functional valuation:
`functional_balance_minor` is `null` on a single-currency grain (the
`?valuation=functional` read falls back to `balance_minor` by identity, P1
decision 8).

functional_balance_minor.description:
Functional-currency carried balance; `null` on a single-currency grain
(functional ≡ transaction).

functional_currency.description:
Functional currency of `functional_balance_minor`; `null` on a
single-currency grain.

if_match.description:
The value state tag the caller last read for this scope — for a revert,
the tag of the row being cleared — or the literal `absent` for a first
write. Required in effect: a change that omits it is rejected on its
own with `if_match_required` while the rest of the batch proceeds. It
is optional in the schema only so that one missing tag refuses one
change instead of the whole request.

op.description:
`set` or `revert`; absent is `set`, so a client written before the
field existed sends exactly what it sent before. An unrecognised word
refuses this change alone with `invalid`.

tenant.description: The target tenant; absent, the caller's own.

value.description:
The new value, carried by a `set` and absent from a `revert`; a
mismatch either way refuses this change alone with `invalid`. For a
`secret`-trait setting this may instead be `{ "pending_id": "…" }`,
naming a secret staged earlier through `/secret-stage`: the staged
entry is adopted and nothing is stored a second time. Any other shape
is a value and validates as one — an explicit `null` included, which
is a value and not the field's absence.

BatchGetItemDto.description: One key in a batch read.

entity_key.description:
A canonical GTS identifier or a Registry Reference UUID, classified exactly
as `GET /entities/{entity_key}` classifies its path segment.

if_none_match.description:
A prior `etag` for this key and `$select`; a match returns `unchanged`.
Batch validators are per item. Exactly one entity-tag, weak or strong:
`*`, an unquoted value or a list is refused rather than read as no condition.

BatchGetRequest.description:
A batch read. Unknown fields are refused, so a misspelled `$select` is not
answered with the default set.

$select.description:
Fields to return for every key, spelled as the GET routes' `$select`.
Absent is the document-free default.

items.description:
No `max_items`: the ceiling is `MAX_BATCH_GET_KEYS`, applied while the body
is parsed. Items past it are counted, not kept.

BatchItemDto.description: One entry of a batch answer.

oneOf.description: The change, when committed.

error.description:
Why, when rejected — one of a fixed vocabulary: `invalid`,
`if_match_required`, `stale`, `conflict`, `forbidden`, `retired`,
`not_found`, `unavailable` or `error`.
`retired` also covers a declaration retired after the client assembled
the change: the check runs again as each change commits.

changes.description: At most five hundred changes, evaluated in order.

BatchResultDto.description: A batch answer: one entry per change.

change_set_id.description: The change set every committed change carries.

BillRunFinishedRequest.description:
`POST /ledger/control/bill-run-finished` request body: the owning
Orchestration's bill-run completion assertion for `(tenant, period)`.

finished.description: `true` once the period's bill run has finished (the close-gate prerequisite).

tenant_id.description: The seller tenant whose ledger this feeds; the PEP gate target. In the body.

Capability.description:
PEP-level capability declarations.

Tells the PDP which advanced features the PEP can handle so the PDP
can tailor its response accordingly.

**Note:** `GroupMembership` and `GroupHierarchy` require access to the
Resource Group tables (`resource_group`, `resource_group_membership`, `resource_group_closure`).
Services that can join against these tables may declare the capabilities;
the PDP will then return `InGroup`/`InGroupSubtree` predicates directly.
Each capable [`crate::pep::ResourceType`] must explicitly enable native
group predicates, use an exact canonical GTS type path as its resource name,
and support the `id` property. The enforcer uses that same type to qualify
RG membership rows and suppresses group capabilities when any prerequisite
is absent. Services without table access should omit these capabilities —
the PDP will degrade group predicates to explicit `In` with pre-resolved IDs.

CategoryDto.description:
A category as returned to a caller.

Field naming is `snake_case`, applied by `#[toolkit_macros::api_dto]` rather
than chosen here: every gear's DTOs serialize the same way, so a client does
not have to know which service produced a payload.

domain_affinity.description: Optional domain this category belongs to.

id.description: Server-assigned identity, stable across a rename.

key.description: The stable slug that becomes a setting key's category segment.

ChangeRecognitionScheduleRequest.description:
The `POST /recognition-schedules/{schedule_id}/changes` request body: change or
cancel an ASC 606 recognition schedule (design §3.6 / §4.6). `{schedule_id}`
(the ACTIVE schedule to change) comes from the PATH; the target seller ledger
is the body's own `tenant_id` (tenant in body, not path — the vhp-core REST
convention); the `(entry, post)` PEP gate authorizes it (a change marks/mints
schedule state). `change_id` is the idempotency key (a replay returns the prior
result, minting no second schedule). `action` is `"cancel"` | `"replace"`.
`treatment` is the upstream modification-accounting decision: `"prospective"` /
`"separate_contract"` apply; `"catch_up"` / unknown is rejected
`MODIFICATION_TREATMENT_REVIEW` (the ledger never silently treats a
modification as prospective). `new_segments` is required for a `replace` (the
NEW version's plan of the remaining deferred), ignored for a `cancel`.

change_id.description: The change idempotency key — a replay returns the prior result.

new_segments.description:
The replacement segments for a `replace` (the new version's plan of the
remaining deferred); omit for a `cancel`.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose schedule this changes; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

ChangeSegmentDto.description:
One replacement recognition segment on a `replace` change (Group H). Maps to
the SDK [`bss_ledger_sdk::ChangeSegment`]; ignored on a `cancel`.

period_id.description: Fiscal `period_id` (`YYYYMM`) this replacement segment recognizes into.

CheckAppDto.description: GitHub-shaped `app` that produced a check run.

CheckRunOutputDto.description: GitHub-shaped `output` of a check run, without the annotation bodies.

CheckSuiteRefDto.description: GitHub-shaped `check_suite` back-reference of a check run.

ChildConversionRequestDto.description:
Response projection for the parent-side conversion REST surface
(`/child-conversions` family). Minimal cross-barrier projection per
`dod-managed-self-managed-modes-parent-side-minimal-surface`: every
field is derivable from the conversion row itself or the converting
tenant's own row (`child_tenant_name`); no closure / metadata /
inventory data leaks across the parent-child barrier.

`request_id` is the conversion row's id (the parent-side projection
renames it to make the cross-barrier minimal contract explicit on
the wire — the field set is what the parent is allowed to see).

Citation.description: A citation extracted from provider annotations.

attachment_id.description: The attachment UUID (the provider file id before mapping).

CitationSource.description: Whether a citation came from a file or web search.

from.description: The source tenant; absent, the caller's own tenant.

disposition.description:
Customer-balance disposition election — recorded when closing with a
positive balance (design 01 §4.2).

CommitDto.description:
GitHub-shaped commit. The list endpoint leaves `stats` and `files`
out, matching GitHub; the single-commit endpoint fills them in.

CommitFileDto.description: A mirrored changed file of a commit, served by the extended API.

CommitStatsDto.description: GitHub `stats` object of a commit detail response.

Constraint.description:
A constraint on a specific resource property.

Multiple constraints within a response are `ORed`:
a resource matches if it satisfies ANY constraint.

predicates.description:
The predicates within this constraint. All predicates are `ANDed`:
a resource matches this constraint only if ALL predicates are satisfied.

login.description: Omitted for anonymous contributors, matching GitHub's shape.

roles.description:
Beyond GitHub's shape: the capacities this person was seen in, and
the window they were seen across.

ControlFeedAck.description:
Ack for a control-feed push: the feed + the `(tenant, period)` grain it landed
on. The push is last-writer-wins, so a re-push of the same grain overwrites.

feed.description: The control feed the push landed on (e.g. `issued-invoice-manifest`).

ConversionPatchDto.description:
Request body for
`PATCH /tenants/{tenant_id}/conversions/{request_id}` and
`PATCH /tenants/{tenant_id}/child-conversions/{request_id}`.

`status` is required and narrowed to the three admissible terminal
transitions ([`ConversionPatchStatusDto`]). `comment` is optional
and follows the same length contract as the POST body.

The handler routes each admissible status to the matching service
method (`approve` / `cancel` / `reject`) — the wire DTO does NOT
know about the service handle. See
[`crate::api::rest::handlers::conversions`] for the dispatch.

comment.description:
Optional caller-supplied rationale. Same `1..=1000` chars
contract as [`RequestOwnConversionDto::comment`]; persisted
to the per-transition column matching the chosen `status`
(`approved_comment` / `cancelled_comment` / `rejected_comment`).

ConversionPatchStatusDto.description:
Admissible terminal transitions for PATCH (approved | cancelled |
rejected). `pending` is reached only via POST initiation; `expired` is
reaper-owned, so a caller `PATCH`ing to it would falsify `actor_kind`.

ConversionSideDto.description:
Wire-shape enum for `initiator_side` on every conversion-request
response. Mirrors [`ConversionSide`] one-to-one. Response-only — a
caller never supplies `initiator_side` on the request body (the
service derives it from the URL collection per the `caller`).

ConversionStatusDto.description:
Wire-shape enum for the conversion-request lifecycle status on
every read surface (`OwnConversionRequestDto`,
`ChildConversionRequestDto`). Mirrors
[`ConversionStatus`] one-to-one. Defined locally on the wire so the
served `OpenAPI` carries the explicit `pending | approved |
cancelled | rejected | expired` enum rather than `String`.

CreateCategoryRequest.description: What a caller supplies to create a category.

key.description:
The stable slug. Validated before anything else touches it: 1 to 128
characters, a GTS segment token — a lowercase letter or `_` first, then
lowercase letters, digits and `_` — since every setting key declared
under the category is composed around it.

sort_order.description: Ordering weight; defaults to 0 as DESIGN.md §4.7 specifies.

CreateChatReq.description: Request DTO for creating a new chat.

CreateCityReq.description: REST DTO for creating a new city

CreateDeclarationRequest.description:
What an administrator supplies to declare a setting.

The key is not among the fields: the service composes it from the vendor,
the category's slug and the leaf name, so a caller cannot mint a key that
disagrees with where the setting is filed. `default_value` is mandatory --
it is what makes resolution total -- and a setting with no meaningful
default sends JSON `null` on a type that admits it; omitting the field is a
different thing and is refused.

anonymous_exposable.description:
Whether the effective value may be served unauthenticated; `false` when
absent, and refused on a `pii` or `secret` setting.

category_id.description: The category the setting is filed under; its slug rides in the key.

data_classification.description:
`public` or `pii`; `secret` is derived from the value type's trait and
is refused here.

default_value.description:
The Schema Default. Mandatory, and an empty placeholder for a secret.
Kept as the request's own text until it is judged: a decimal a double
cannot hold exactly is refused `value_not_canonical`, as a value write
refuses it, and only the text can tell — once parsed, the literal is
already the nearest double.

licence_feature.description: Optional licence feature gating the setting in R2.

name.description: The leaf name: the last segment of the key, unique in the category.

requires_step_up.description:
Whether a write needs a fresh re-authentication; the protective `true`
when absent.

value_type_id.description:
The value type the default and every override validate against: one of
the catalogue under `gts.cf.core.settings.type_*~`, or a registered
module-owned one.

vendor.description: The vendor segment of the composed key.

idempotency_key.description:
Optional idempotency key for deduplication of retried requests.
Within the same `(owner_kind, owner_id)`, a retry with the same key
returns the original response without creating a new file.

@cpt-cf-file-storage-fr-upload-idempotency

CreateGroupDto.description: REST DTO for creating a new resource group.

id.description: Optional caller-supplied ID. If omitted, the server generates a UUID.

parent_id.description: Parent group ID (null for root groups).

tenant_id.description: Optional target tenant for the created group.

type.description: GTS chained type path. Must have prefix `gts.cf.core.rg.type.v1~`.

CreateRetentionRuleReq.description: Request body to create a retention rule (`POST /retention-rules`).

scope_target_id.description: Target id (`user_id` for user scope, `file_id` for file scope; omit for tenant scope).

CreateSecretRequestDto.description:
Request body for `POST /credstore/v1/secrets`.

`Debug` is hand-written to redact `value` — a derived `Debug` would expose
the plaintext secret if this DTO is ever `{:?}`-logged by a future layer.

expires_at.description: Expiry instant (RFC 3339); only for expirable types.

type.description:
Secret type as a full GTS type id (built-in or custom); defaults to
the generic type. Resolved and existence-checked against the
types-registry.

value.description: Secret value as a UTF-8 string.

CreateTypeDto.description: REST DTO for creating a new GTS type.

allowed_membership_types.description: GTS type paths of allowed membership resource types.

allowed_parent_types.description: GTS type paths of allowed parent types.

can_be_root.description: Whether groups of this type can be root nodes.

code.description:
GTS type path. Must have prefix `gts.cf.core.rg.type.v1~`.

Whether the type creates a new tenant scope is derived from the code:
any path starting with the tenant RG type prefix is a tenant type.

metadata_schema.description: Optional JSON Schema for instance metadata.

CreateUsageRecordRequest.description:
Per-record create payload. Carries `gts_id` as a permissive `String`
(same rationale as [`CreateUsageTypeRequest`]) so a bad-prefix value
surfaces as the per-record `Problem` instead of axum's default
`text/plain` 422 for the entire batch. per-record problem envelopes
still surface for closed-shape membership, size-cap, and key
validation. Intentionally has no identity field: `id` is
gateway-derived via `usage_collector_sdk::derive_usage_record_id`,
mirroring the `UsageRecord::id` doc.

corrects_id.description:
When set, marks this submission as a counter compensation
referencing a previously emitted ordinary usage row. Absent on
ordinary submissions. The four-cell value matrix and L1 referential
rule are enforced at the gateway per
`cpt-cf-usage-collector-algo-usage-emission-semantics-enforcement-on-ingest-v2`.

idempotency_key.description:
Mandatory caller-supplied idempotency key per
`cpt-cf-usage-collector-dod-usage-emission-fr-idempotency`. The
plugin SPI dedups every persisted record on
`(tenant_id, gts_id, idempotency_key, created_at)` (ADR-0014); a
missing key surfaces as a request-deserialization failure.

CreateUsageRecordResultDto.description:
Per-record outcome inside [`CreateUsageRecordsResponse`]. Externally
tagged on `outcome` (snake-case via the `api_dto`-applied `rename_all`)
so accepted and rejected records share a uniform envelope keyed by
input order. An accepted entry carries the persisted record body; a
rejected entry carries the per-record canonical `Problem` body
verbatim — the same envelope a single-record failure would surface,
folded into the batch response.

CreateUsageRecordsResponse.description:
Batch create response body. `results` preserves input order; a partial
failure surfaces as HTTP `207 Multi-Status` with per-record `Rejected`
entries (callers must inspect each `outcome`).

CreateUsageTypeRequest.description:
Register-request body for `POST /usage-collector/v1/usage-types`.

Carries `gts_id` as a permissive `String` rather than the validating
[`usage_collector_sdk::UsageTypeGtsId`] newtype so the handler can
synthesise the canonical `invalid_base_gts_id` `Problem` envelope on
rejection — relying on the newtype's `Deserialize` would surface
bad-base payloads as axum's default `text/plain` 422. `kind` is the
closed counter / gauge discriminator carried as `String` for the same
`utoipa`-isolation reason as `gts_id`; the handler parses it through
the SDK [`usage_collector_sdk::UsageKind`] enum so unknown values are
rejected (per ADR-0012 amendment 2026-06-08).

CreateUserReq.description: REST DTO for creating a new user

id.description: Optional ID for the user. If not provided, a UUID v7 will be generated

allOf.description: The declaration now live at the key.

evolved.description:
`true` when the setting's active declaration changed its value type,
Schema Default or scope class and this call evolved it: the declaration
returned is the next major, under a new `key`, holding every value of
the previous one re-validated, and the previous major is retired.

reactivated.description:
`true` when the key held a retired declaration that this call revived,
with its retained values re-entering resolution.

CreatedDeclarationDto.description:
The response to a create: the declaration, and whether a retired one was
revived or the active one evolved rather than a new setting declared.

CreditApplicationRequest.description:
The `POST /credit-applications` request body: ONE wire shape for both wallet
kinds, discriminated by `kind` (`"grant"` | `"apply"`). The target seller
ledger is the body's own `tenant_id` (tenant in body, not path — the vhp-core
REST convention); the `(credit_application, write)` PEP gate authorizes it.
`scale` is advisory; the ledger resolves the authoritative per-line scale.

The kind-specific fields are all optional on the wire and validated in
[`Self::into_sdk`]: a `grant` requires `amount_minor` + `credit_grant_event_type`
(and ignores `targets`); an `apply` requires a non-empty `targets` (and ignores
the grant fields). A missing required field or an unknown `kind` is rejected
`400 InvalidArgument` before the SDK type is built.

amount_minor.description:
Grant only: amount to park into the wallet, in minor units. Required for
`kind = "grant"`, ignored for `"apply"`.

credit_application_id.description: The `CREDIT_APPLY` idempotency business id (a replay returns the prior post).

credit_grant_event_type.description:
Grant only: the wallet sub-grain bucket the credit accrues to. Required for
`kind = "grant"`, ignored for `"apply"`.

kind.description: The wallet operation: `"grant"` (park pool cash) | `"apply"` (spend wallet).

scale.description: Advisory currency scale; the ledger resolves the authoritative one.

targets.description:
Apply only: the per-invoice receivable shares to spend the wallet against
(validated against the payer's open AR). Required (non-empty) for
`kind = "apply"`, ignored for `"grant"`.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this posts into; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

CreditApplicationResponse.description:
The `POST /credit-applications` response: the posting handle plus — for an
apply — the per-sub-grain wallet draw-downs (`debits`) and the per-invoice
receivable shares (`applications`). A grant leaves both vecs empty (it moves
no wallet/AR splits). Always `201` (the wallet post is never an idempotent
`200`-replay at the handler — a replay returns the prior `posting` with
`replayed = true`).

CreditApplicationShareDto.description:
One per-invoice receivable share in a credit-application apply response: how
much of the wallet was applied to `invoice_id`. A row of
[`CreditApplicationResponse::applications`] (empty for a grant). Mirrors the
SDK's reuse of `AllocationSplit` on the apply side.

CreditDebitDto.description:
One per-sub-grain wallet draw-down in a credit-application response: how much
the apply drew from the `credit_grant_event_type` bucket. A row of
[`CreditApplicationResponse::debits`] (empty for a grant).

CreditNoteRequest.description:
The `POST /credit-notes` request body: a compensating credit note against a
posted invoice (design §4.2). The target seller ledger is the body's own
`tenant_id` (tenant in body, not path — the vhp-core REST convention); the
`(entry, post)` PEP gate authorizes it (a credit note posts a balanced
compensating journal entry — the same data-plane post action as the
recognition run / invoice post). Idempotent on `credit_note_id` (the
`(tenant, CREDIT_NOTE, credit_note_id)` engine claim): a replay returns the
prior posting with `replayed = true`.

`amount_minor` is **incl-tax**; `tax_minor` is the reversed-tax slice of it;
`requested_deferred_minor` is the **split intent** — how much of the ex-tax
revenue portion (`amount_minor − tax_minor`) targets the unreleased deferred
balance (the rest reduces recognized revenue). `goodwill = true` ⇒ an AR-only
goodwill credit (debits `GOODWILL`, touches no schedule, MUST carry
`requested_deferred_minor = 0`). A malformed shape (negative amounts, tax over
amount, deferred over ex-tax, empty reason, goodwill-with-deferred) is rejected
`400` (`AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE` / `InvalidArgument`) by the domain `validate_shape`;
an indeterminable split is `CREDIT_NOTE_SPLIT_AMBIGUOUS`; an over-headroom note
is `CREDIT_NOTE_EXCEEDS_HEADROOM`.

amount_minor.description: The note amount **incl-tax**, in minor units (`>= 0`, `> 0` enforced).

credit_note_id.description:
The `(tenant, CREDIT_NOTE, credit_note_id)` idempotency business id + the
`credit_note` row PK.

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency of the note (all legs share it).

goodwill.description:
`true` ⇒ an AR-only goodwill credit (`GOODWILL`, no schedule reduction);
`None` ⇒ `false`.

origin_invoice_id.description:
The originating posted invoice the note credits (its rows are never
mutated).

origin_invoice_item_ref.description:
The targeted posted invoice-item ref (the line being credited); `None` for
an invoice-level credit.

payer_tenant_id.description: The tenant the original invoice billed (the AR / wallet owner).

po_allocation_group.description:
The PO / allocation group the targeted line books under (the split-basis
dimension); `None` for a line with no group.

reason_code.description:
The mandatory business reason code (AC #14) recorded on the `credit_note`
row.

requested_deferred_minor.description:
The split **intent**: how much of the ex-tax revenue amount targets the
unreleased deferred balance (`0 <= … <= amount_minor − tax_minor`). MUST be
`0` when `goodwill` is set.

revenue_stream.description: The revenue stream the credit books against (per-stream legs carry it).

scale.description: Advisory currency scale; the ledger resolves the authoritative one.

tax.description:
The authoritative tax breakdown — one component per `(jurisdiction,
filing-period, rate)`, each reversing onto its OWN `TAX_PAYABLE` leg so
`tax_subbalance` disaggregates (§4.5). Empty ⇒ a single dimensionless tax leg
from `tax_minor` (legacy). A non-empty breakdown MUST sum to `tax_minor` (a
`400` otherwise); `tax_minor` stays the split scalar.

tax_minor.description:
The tax slice of `amount_minor` to reverse onto `TAX_PAYABLE` (`>= 0`,
`<= amount_minor`).

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this posts into; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

CreditNoteResponse.description:
The `POST /credit-notes` response: a reference to the compensating-entry
posting. A fresh post renders `201`, an idempotent replay `200` (the handler
reads `replayed`). Mirrors [`PostingRefDto`].

CreditNoteView.description:
The `GET /credit-notes` / `GET /credit-notes/{creditNoteId}` response: the
recorded credit note (Phase 1b / read-surface §5). Drawn from the
`credit_note` row (the `(tenant, credit_note_id)` grain). `amount_minor` is
incl-tax; `recognized_part_minor` + `deferred_part_minor` are the ex-tax split
parts and do NOT sum to `amount_minor` (no CHECK — they mirror the entity).
Tenant-scoped (SQL-level BOLA): an unknown credit note — or one outside the
caller's subtree — yields a `404` (no existence leak). Mirrors [`RefundView`].

deferred_part_minor.description: The ex-tax deferred part of the split.

origin_invoice_item_ref.description: The originating invoice item the note targets (`None` when whole-invoice).

recognized_part_minor.description:
The ex-tax recognized part of the split (does NOT sum with the deferred
part to `amount_minor`).

split_basis_ref.description:
The schedule/split basis the `RecognizedDeferredSplitter` keyed on
(`None` when the split needed no schedule basis).

CurrencyScaleDto.description: One non-ISO currency-scale row to seed.

plausible_max_major.description:
Per-currency plausible maximum in MAJOR units; omit for the default
`10^12` (max scale 6). A higher-precision currency (e.g. BTC scale 8)
passes a smaller cap (e.g. `21_000_000`) so its scale fits `i64` headroom.

DebitNoteRequest.description:
The `POST /debit-notes` request body: an *additional charge* against a posted
invoice — a DIRECT split mirroring the Slice-1 invoice-post (design §4.3). The
target seller ledger is the body's own `tenant_id` (tenant in body, not path);
the `(entry, post)` PEP gate authorizes it. Idempotent on `debit_note_id` (the
`(tenant, DEBIT_NOTE, debit_note_id)` engine claim): a replay returns the prior
posting with `replayed = true`. A debit note **raises** the invoice's headroom
(`debit_note_total_minor += amount`); it cannot trip the headroom cap.

`amount_minor` is **incl-tax** (the single DR `AR`); `tax_minor` is the posted
tax evidence (CR `TAX_PAYABLE`, never recomputed); `deferred_minor` is how much
of the ex-tax revenue portion (`amount_minor − tax_minor`) defers to
`CONTRACT_LIABILITY` (the rest recognizes now to `REVENUE`). When
`deferred_minor > 0` the `recognition` spec drives the schedule build (D4 — the
SAME `ScheduleBuilder` path the invoice-post uses) and is REQUIRED (a deferred
note with no spec is a `400`). A malformed shape is rejected `400` by the
domain `validate_shape`; a closed payer is `PAYER_CLOSED`.

amount_minor.description:
The note amount **incl-tax**, in minor units (`>= 0`, `> 0` enforced) — the
single DR `AR`.

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency of the note (all legs share it).

debit_note_id.description:
The `(tenant, DEBIT_NOTE, debit_note_id)` idempotency business id + the
`debit_note` row PK.

deferred_minor.description:
How much of the ex-tax revenue amount is deferred to `CONTRACT_LIABILITY`
(`0 <= … <= amount_minor − tax_minor`); the rest recognizes now. `0` ⇒ fully
recognized (no `CONTRACT_LIABILITY` line, no schedule build).

origin_invoice_id.description:
The originating posted invoice (whose headroom this raises; its rows are
never mutated).

origin_invoice_item_ref.description:
The targeted posted invoice-item ref — anchors the freshly-built schedule's
NOT-NULL `source_invoice_item_ref` when the note defers (§4.7). Required
(non-empty) for a deferred note; optional (lineage only) otherwise.

payer_tenant_id.description: The tenant the original invoice billed (the AR owner the charge lands on).

reason_code.description: The mandatory business reason / context code (AC #14). Non-empty.

oneOf.description:
The ASC 606 recognition spec (Slice 4 — the SAME shape the invoice-post
item carries). REQUIRED when `deferred_minor > 0` (drives the schedule
build, D4); `None` for a fully-recognized note.

revenue_stream.description: The revenue stream the charge books against (per-stream legs carry it).

scale.description: Advisory currency scale; the ledger resolves the authoritative one.

tax.description:
The authoritative tax breakdown — one component per `(jurisdiction,
filing-period, rate)`, each posting onto its OWN `TAX_PAYABLE` leg so
`tax_subbalance` disaggregates (§4.5). Empty ⇒ a single dimensionless tax leg
from `tax_minor` (legacy). A non-empty breakdown MUST sum to `tax_minor` (a
`400` otherwise); `tax_minor` stays the split scalar.

tax_minor.description:
The tax slice of `amount_minor` posted onto `TAX_PAYABLE` (`>= 0`,
`<= amount_minor`). Posted tax evidence — never recomputed.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this posts into; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

DebitNoteResponse.description:
The `POST /debit-notes` response: a reference to the direct-split posting. A
fresh post renders `201`, an idempotent replay `200`. Mirrors [`PostingRefDto`].

DebitNoteView.description:
The `GET /debit-notes` / `GET /debit-notes/{debitNoteId}` response: the
recorded debit note — an additional charge (Phase 1b / read-surface §5). Drawn
from the `debit_note` row (the `(tenant, debit_note_id)` grain). `amount_minor`
is incl-tax; `recognized_part_minor` + `deferred_part_minor` are the ex-tax
split parts and do NOT sum to `amount_minor` (no CHECK). The `debit_note`
table is leaner than `credit_note` (NO `revenue_stream` / `reason_code` /
item ref). Tenant-scoped (SQL-level BOLA): an unknown debit note — or one
outside the caller's subtree — yields a `404` (no existence leak). Mirrors
[`CreditNoteView`].

deferred_part_minor.description: The ex-tax deferred part of the split.

recognized_part_minor.description: The ex-tax recognized part of the split.

actor_name.description:
The current name of `actor` (P-D-262): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

DeclarationDto.description:
A declaration as returned to a caller.

Carries `key`, `value_type_id` and the resolved trait set, which is what the
read surface is specified to render. The value type travels beside the key
because the key no longer carries it: a setting key is a GTS *type* id
(ADR-002), and which value type its default and overrides validate against
is a separate fact of the declaration, not a half of its name.

anonymous_exposable.description: Whether the anonymous surface may show the value.

data_classification.description: `public`, `pii` or `secret`; `secret` is derived from the value type.

default_value.description: The Schema Default every resolution chain ends in.

domain_affinity.description: The administrative domain, when the declaration is bound to one.

etag.description: The declaration's state tag, also sent as the `ETag` header.

has_secret_trait.description: Whether the value type carries the `secret` trait.

id.description: Server-assigned identity, stable across a re-key.

last_change_at.description: When the definition last changed, RFC 3339.

leaf_slug.description: The setting's own name slug, unique within its category.

licence_feature.description:
The licence feature that will gate this declaration once the License
Resolver exists. Reported, not enforced.

owner_module.description: The contributing module, for module-contributed declarations.

requires_step_up.description: Whether a value write needs a fresh re-authentication.

traits.description:
The value type's effective traits, merged across its inheritance chain.

An empty object when the registry could not answer. Always present so a
client renders the same shape either way rather than branching on
absence.

value_type_id.description: GTS id of the value type the default and every override validate against.

DeleteEntitiesRequest.description: A deletion batch. Unknown fields are rejected to prevent ignored safety options.

dry_run.description: Predict without changing entities. Defaults to `false`; part of the idempotency fingerprint.

items.description: Runtime configuration supplies the batch limit.

DeleteEntityDto.description: A batch deletion target, resolved like `GET /entities/{entity_key}`.

entity_key.description: A canonical GTS identifier or a Registry Reference UUID.

expected_resource_version.description: Required positive version; optional internally for uniform validation errors.

entity_key.description:
The target's key, whether or not it named an entity: a GTS identifier as
the request spelled it (only the canonical spelling is accepted), or a
Registry Reference in canonical lowercase hyphenated form, however the
request spelled the UUID.

oneOf.description: Present when this target failed.

DeletionKindDto.description: The discriminator of a deletion operation.

status.description:
Progress only — the outcomes are on the items and are deliberately not
aggregated here.

DenyReason.description: Reason for an explicit deny from the PDP.

DisputePhaseQueuedResponse.description:
The `POST /disputes/{dispute_id}/phases` response when the phase was an
out-of-order `won`/`lost` whose `opened` has not landed: the request was
durably QUEUED for a later drain (HTTP 202 Accepted), not posted. `status` is
the fixed `dispute-phase-queued` token; `flow` + `business_id` are the queue
key and `queued_at` the intake instant. No posting handle — nothing has posted
yet. Mirrors `AllocationQueuedResponse`.

queued_at.description: When the intake durably enqueued the request.

status.description: Always `dispute-phase-queued` (a normal-body kebab-case token, not an error).

DisputeView.description:
The `GET /disputes` / `GET /disputes/{disputeId}` response: the chargeback
dispute's current state (read-surface R3). Drawn from the `ledger_dispute` row
(the `(tenant, dispute_id)` grain) — its chosen `variant` (`CASH_HOLD` /
`AR_RECLASS`), the current `cycle` + `last_phase` (`OPENED` / `WON` / `LOST`),
the `disputed_amount_minor`, and the `cash_hold_minor` actually moved into
`DISPUTE_HOLD` at open (`0` for `AR_RECLASS`). The persisted `version` (the
optimistic-concurrency counter) is INTERNAL and not surfaced. Tenant-scoped
(SQL-level BOLA): an unknown dispute — or one outside the caller's subtree —
yields a `404` (no existence leak). Mirrors [`RefundView`].

cash_hold_minor.description:
The cash held in `DISPUTE_HOLD` at open (`0` for `AR_RECLASS`) — the size
the `won`/`lost` outcome releases / forfeits.

cycle.description: The dispute cycle (re-opens advance it; the `last_phase` is at this cycle).

last_phase.description: The latest phase recorded on this dispute (`OPENED` / `WON` / `LOST`).

variant.description:
The chosen variant (`CASH_HOLD` ⇒ cash moved to `DISPUTE_HOLD` at open /
`AR_RECLASS` ⇒ AR reclassed `ACTIVE`→`DISPUTED`, no cash leg).

DocumentHistoryDto.description:
The full posting history of one source document, the
`GET …/audit/documents/{sourceDocType}/{sourceBusinessId}/history` response:
every entry for that document plus any reversal / mapping-correction that
links to one of them, ordered by `created_seq`.

DualControlPolicyResponse.description:
The written dual-control policy version (the minted `version` + the thresholds
it carries; the resolver picks the latest `effective_from`).

DualControlPolicyView.description:
The `GET /dual-control-policy` response (read-surface): the tenant's EFFECTIVE
dual-control threshold policy — the version in force now (greatest
`effective_from <= now`, highest `version` on a tie), or the ratified platform
defaults when the tenant has set no policy row. `is_default` is `true` in the
latter case (`version` / `effective_from` are then `None`). Tenant-scoped
(SQL-level BOLA): a tenant outside the caller's subtree reads as the platform
defaults — the thresholds are public constants, so no existence/value leak.

a6_backdating_biz_days.description: The A6 material-backdating window in business days.

d2_threshold_minor.description:
The D2 amount threshold in USD-equivalent minor units: a governed money-out
/ grant at or above this needs preparer→approver sign-off.

effective_from.description:
The `effective_from` instant of the version in force (`None` when the
platform defaults apply — the tenant has no row).

is_default.description:
`true` when no tenant row applies and these are the ratified platform
defaults; `false` when a configured version is in force.

pending_ttl_seconds.description:
The TTL (seconds) a fresh `PENDING` / `NEEDS_REWORK` approval lives before
it expires.

version.description: The `version` number in force (`None` when the platform defaults apply).

EffectiveAccessDto.description: The effective access and where it comes from.

supplied_by.description: The tenant whose row supplies it; absent for `overridable`.

EffectivePolicyDto.description:
Effective policy response: the most-restrictive combination of tenant ⊕ user.

@cpt-cf-file-storage-usecase-configure-policy

allowed_mime_types.description: Intersection of allowed mime types from all levels (`null` = all types permitted).

max_bytes.description: Effective global size limit in bytes (`null` = unlimited).

metadata_limits.description: Effective metadata limits (most restrictive per field).

per_mime_max_bytes.description: Per-mime size overrides (union from all levels, most restrictive per pattern).

EffectiveValueDto.description:
The effective value at a scope, as `GET /settings-service/v1/settings/{key}`
returns it.

etag.description:
The value state tag of the requested scope's own row, or of the absent
state — what a write at this scope presents in `If-Match`. Also sent as
the `ETag` header.

fallback.description:
What this scope resolves to without a row of its own — the nearest
valid ancestor override, else the Schema Default — masked by the same
rule as `value`. Equal to `value` when the scope holds no override: the
settings table's *Default* column, and what a revert would leave.

fallback_scope.description: The scope that supplies the fallback; absent for a Schema Default.

inheritance_trail.description: The scopes inspected, root to self, with setter identity.

last_change_at.description:
Recency of the effective value the caller sees: the later of the
declaration's own change and the resolved row's.

masked.description:
Whether `value` and `fallback` carry the mask token rather than the
value: one decision, made on the declaration's classification, for
both.

needs_review.description:
Present when the requested scope's own override is flagged for review;
the value above is then the fallthrough the resolver served.

needs_review_detail.description: Why the own override is flagged.

source_scope.description: The scope that supplied the value; absent for a Schema Default.

tenant_id.description:
The requested scope as a tenant id; the root tenant's id is platform
scope.

traits.description: The value type's resolved trait set.

value.description: The resolved value, masked by classification.

EntityDto.description:
One entity, projected by `$select` (SPEC §10.2).

`gts_id`, `gts_uuid`, `kind` and `lifecycle_status` are always present, so a
projected item is identifiable, its kind needs no second read, and a tombstone is
never mistaken for an absence. An
unselected field is omitted; a selected document that is JSON `null` stays
present as `null`. The three artifacts are absent on an Instance. Documents
are written as stored, canonical text: keys sorted, no insignificant whitespace.

content.description: The whole authored document, either kind.

gts_uuid.description:
Always present. The Registry Reference: a deterministic `UUIDv5` of the
identifier.

lifecycle_status.description: Always present. A tombstone stays exact-readable and is listed only on request.

EntityLookupDto.description:
One key's answer, echoing the key it was asked by.

The echo is not redundant: batch order is not contractual, so a caller matches
answers to questions by it, and an absence has no entity to carry the key for
it. A caller normalizes its own UUID keys before matching. A Registry Reference is echoed
lowercase and hyphenated however the request spelled it, as an operation
echoes it; an identifier is echoed as sent.

oneOf.description:
The selected fields, exactly as the exact read returns them for the same
`$select`. Present only on `found`.

etag.description:
The validator for this key under this `$select`, byte-identical to the exact
read's `ETag`. Present unless `not_found`.

EntityLookupStatusDto.description:
`found`, `unchanged` or `not_found`.

DESIGN's `failed` needs federation, which is out of P0 (SPEC §2); declaring it
would publish a value this gear never emits.

EntityLookupsDto.description: One answer per distinct key in a batch read. Result order is not contractual.

EntityPageDto.description: One bounded page of discovery results (SPEC §10.1's `EntityPage`).

items.description: Each item projected exactly as the exact read projects it.

EntryAnnotationRequestDto.description:
The `PATCH /journal-entries/{entryId}/annotation` request body (Group 2B,
Variant C): set the typed controlled non-financial `description` note on the
entry (or one of its lines). `description` is screened for raw customer PII
before any write (`PII_IN_METADATA_VALUE`); `null` clears the note.

description.description: The controlled note. `null` clears it. Screened for raw customer PII.

reason.description: Audit reason for the change (recorded on the secured-audit record).

target_line_id.description: The target line id when `target_kind = "LINE"`; ignored for `ENTRY`.

EntryDto.description:
A read-back journal entry (header + its lines), the `GET
/journal-entries/{entryId}` response. Carries the audit dims
(`posted_at_utc`, `posted_by_actor_id`, `origin`, `correlation_id`) +
`reverses_entry_id` a caller needs to audit / build a reversal.

EntryHeaderView.description:
One row of the `GET /journal-entries` header list (read-surface R5). A
LIGHTWEIGHT projection of a `journal_entry` HEADER — the entry coordinate +
audit dims a caller filters / cross-cuts on (`source_doc_type` ⇒ all
`MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` / `REFUND` / `CREDIT_NOTE` entries, `source_business_id`
⇒ all entries of one business document, `period_id` ⇒ all entries of a
period). Carries NO lines and NONE of the tamper-evidence hash-chain fields
(`row_hash` / `prev_hash` / `prev_entry_id` / `prev_period_id` are chain
internals); a caller that needs the lines reads the full entry via
`GET /journal-entries/{entryId}` (which returns the richer [`EntryDto`]).
Drawn from the `journal_entry` row (the `(entry_id, tenant_id, period_id)`
grain; `entry_id` is the default keyset-order column). Tenant-scoped
(SQL-level BOLA): the page never contains a foreign-tenant header (no
existence leak). Mirrors [`RefundView`].

created_seq.description: The DB-assigned per-tenant monotonic posting sequence.

entry_currency.description: The entry's booking currency (the header-level currency).

origin.description: The posting origin (the channel / driver that emitted the entry).

period_id.description: The fiscal period (`YYYYMM`) the entry posted into.

reverses_entry_id.description:
The reversed entry id when this header is itself a reversal (`None`
otherwise).

source_business_id.description: The originating business document id (the invoice / note / refund ref).

source_doc_type.description:
The business document class (`INVOICE_POST` / `MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT` /
`REFUND` / `CREDIT_NOTE` / …) — the primary cross-cut filter dim.

value.description: The value to match (UUID string, plain string, number, bool, etc.).

ErasureRequestDto.description:
`POST …/audit/erasure` request body: the payer to erase. The free-text
investigation reason is the **`X-Investigation-Reason` header** (§5 — the
single source for the reason recorded on the `erasure` record), not a body
field. `target_scope` opens a DIFFERENT tenant's PII map (the cross-tenant
DPO path, §5) — absent or the caller's own ⇒ routine same-tenant erasure; a
different tenant is forensic-gated (authorized for `(entry, erase)` on the
target + a required reason, else `CROSS_TENANT_ACCESS_DENIED` /
`MISSING_INVESTIGATION_REASON`).

target_scope.description: The tenant whose PII map to erase (defaults to the caller's own).

EvaluationRequest.description:
Authorization evaluation request.

Follows the `AuthZEN` 1.0 model: Subject + Action + Resource + Context.

subject.description: The subject (who is making the request).

capabilities.description: PEP capabilities (tells PDP what the PEP can handle).

require_constraints.description:
Whether the PDP should return row-level constraints.
- `true` for LIST/GET/UPDATE/DELETE (need scope filtering)
- `false` for CREATE (just need decision)

supported_properties.description: Supported constraint properties (tells PDP which properties the PEP understands).

oneOf.description: Tenant context for multi-tenant scoping.

EvaluationResponse.description:
Authorization evaluation response.

The PDP returns a decision (allow/deny) and optionally a context
containing constraints or deny reason.

context.description: Response context with constraints or deny reason.

EvaluationResponseContext.description:
Authorization evaluation response context.

Contains constraints (when `decision` is `true`) or deny reason
(when `decision` is `false`).

constraints.description:
Row-level constraints to apply when `decision` is `true`.
Empty when `require_constraints` was `false` or when access is unrestricted.
Multiple constraints are `ORed` (any one matching is sufficient).

oneOf.description: Reason for denial (present when `decision` is `false`).

EventLabelDto.description: GitHub `{ "name": ... }` label reference inside an issue event.

EventMilestoneDto.description: GitHub `{ "title": ... }` milestone reference inside an issue event.

ExceptionView.description: One exception-queue row, projected for the dashboard. PII-free (ids + codes).

FallbackResultDto.description: A revert or remove: the row is gone and the scope falls back.

effective.description: What the scope resolves to now.

FileDto.description: File metadata response (`GET /files/{id}`, and the body of mutations).

FileParserInfoDto.description: REST DTO for file parser info response

functional_currency.description:
The legal entity's functional (books) currency, ISO-4217 (S5-F3); omit for
a single-currency tenant.

FlaggedOverrideDto.description: An override flagged for review, as the needs-review listing reports it.

etag.description:
The override's value state tag — what a write correcting this row
presents in `If-Match`.

needs_review_detail.description: Why the override no longer validates.

set_by.description:
Who set it: an administrator's identity, masked for a caller not
authorized for unmasked PII.

tenant_id.description: The tenant whose override is flagged.

value.description: The stored value, masked by classification.

FreezeDto.description: One scope-freeze row in a tamper-status read.

FxRateIngestRequest.description:
Secondary manual / seed ingest of one FX rate into the local `ledger_fx_rate`
store (the primary path is the `RateProviderV1` plugin pull, design §4.6 /
decision 2). Upsert-keyed on `(tenant_id, base_currency, quote_currency,
provider)`: re-posting the same tuple overwrites the quote (`rate_micro` /
`as_of` / `fallback_order`) — idempotent on `(tenant, base, quote, provider,
as_of)`. `tenant_id` rides the body (the vhp-core write convention, no tenant
in the path).

as_of.description: The publication timestamp that drives the staleness rule.

base_currency.description: Transaction-side ISO-4217 code (the `base` of the `base → quote` rate).

fallback_order.description: The provider's precedence rank (0 = primary); defaults to `0` when omitted.

provider.description: Provider id recorded verbatim (the fallback-order key, e.g. `"ecb"`).

rate_micro.description:

Group membership predicate: resource is visible if it belongs to any of the listed groups.

The PEP compiler uses the current [`crate::pep::ResourceType`]'s canonical
GTS name as the RG member type. `SecureORM` compiles the result to a
type-qualified membership subquery and casts the entity property to text to
match RG's opaque `resource_id` storage. Unless the resource explicitly opts
in with a canonical GTS name, the PEP suppresses the native capability and
the PDP must use an explicit [`InPredicate`] or deny.

InGroupSubtreePredicate.description:
Group subtree predicate: resource is visible if it belongs to any group
that is a descendant of the listed ancestor groups.

The PEP compiler uses the current [`crate::pep::ResourceType`]'s canonical
GTS name as the RG member type. `SecureORM` compiles the result to a
type-qualified membership subquery whose group set comes from
`resource_group_closure`. Unless the resource explicitly opts in with a
canonical GTS name, the PEP suppresses the native capabilities and the PDP
must use an explicit [`InPredicate`] or deny.

ancestor_ids.description: Ancestor group UUIDs - the resource must be a member of any descendant.

property.description:
Resource property to filter. Native compilation currently requires
`pep_properties::RESOURCE_ID`; other properties need a future
per-property RG member-type mapping.

values.description: The set of values to match against.

InTenantSubtreePredicate.description:
Tenant subtree predicate: resource is visible if its tenant property is a
descendant of a single root tenant per the AM-owned `tenant_closure` table.

Compiles to (with `barrier_mode = Respect`, the default):
`property IN (SELECT descendant_id FROM tenant_closure
  WHERE ancestor_id = root_tenant_id AND barrier = 0)`

With `barrier_mode = Ignore`:
`property IN (SELECT descendant_id FROM tenant_closure
  WHERE ancestor_id = root_tenant_id)`

The `barrier = 0` clamp matches the AM closure-table contract:
`barrier` is set when any tenant on the strict path
`(ancestor, descendant]` is `self_managed`. Respecting the barrier
therefore yields the canonical "subtree minus self-managed branches"
semantics; ignoring it is reserved for cross-barrier operations such
as billing or tenant metadata reads.

Multiple-root semantics are expressed at the constraint envelope: emit
one `Constraint` per root and rely on the OR-of-constraints semantics.

**`descendant_status`:** When non-empty, the predicate compiles to
`AND descendant_status IN (...)` on the closure subquery, restricting
the subtree to tenants in the listed statuses. The name mirrors the
`tenant_closure.descendant_status` column so the binding is unambiguous
— the filter applies to the descendants reached via the closure, not
to the ancestor root.

barrier_mode.description:
Barrier enforcement mode. Defaults to [`BarrierMode::Respect`]
which clamps the closure subquery with `AND barrier = 0`.

descendant_status.description:
Status filter applied to the descendants reached via the closure.

Empty list means "no status filter"; a non-empty list compiles to
`AND descendant_status IN (...)` on the closure subquery. The PEP
maps each [`TenantStatus`] to the SMALLINT encoding canonically
defined by [`TenantStatus::as_smallint`] (`Active = 1`,
`Suspended = 2`, `Deleted = 3`).

property.description:
Resource property to filter (e.g., `pep_properties::OWNER_TENANT_ID`,
or `pep_properties::RESOURCE_ID` on the `tenants` entity itself).

root_tenant_id.description: Root tenant UUID — the resource's tenant must be a descendant of this tenant.

caller_can_withdraw.description:

The current name of `submitted_by` (AP-D-11): its display name, else first and last name, else

InvoiceExposureResponse.description:
The `GET /invoices/{invoice_id}/exposure` response: an invoice's credit-note
**headroom** (the `invoice_exposure` counter) plus its **true remaining AR**
(the payment-reduced open receivable, design §4.7). The headroom is the room
left for further credit notes: `remaining_headroom_minor = original_total_minor
+ `debit_note_total_minor` − `credit_note_total_minor`` (the slack in the
``credit_note_total_minor` <= `original_total_minor` + `debit_note_total_minor``
CHECK, AC #24). ``open_ar_minor`` is the SEPARATE current open AR (what a credit
note's `CR AR` leg is capped at before the wallet remainder, K-2) — distinct
from the headroom (which never decreases with payments). Tenant-scoped
(SQL-level BOLA): an invoice with no exposure row yet (no note ever posted) —
or one outside the caller's subtree — yields a `404` (no existence leak).

debit_note_total_minor.description: The running Σ debit-note incl-tax totals (raises the headroom).

open_ar_minor.description:
The invoice's current open AR incl. tax (payment-reduced) — the `CR AR` cap
a credit note fills before spilling to the wallet remainder. SEPARATE from
the headroom.

original_total_minor.description: The seeded original posted AR incl. tax (the headroom basis).

remaining_headroom_minor.description: The remaining credit-note headroom = `original + debit − credit` (`>= 0`).

ManualAdjustmentRequest.description:
The `POST /manual-adjustments` request body: a *governed* manual adjustment
(design §4.6) — the ledger's escape hatch for corrections the typed flows
(invoice / settle / allocate / S3 notes / S4 recognition) do not cover (rounding
residue, suspense / cash-clearing clean-up). The target seller ledger is the
body's own `tenant_id` (tenant in body, not path); the `(entry, post)` PEP gate
authorizes it. Idempotent on `adjustment_id` (the `(tenant, MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT,
adjustment_id)` engine claim): a replay returns the prior posting with `replayed
= true`.

`action` selects a code-owned allow-list of account classes the legs may touch;
`REVENUE` / `CONTRACT_LIABILITY` are globally off-limits and an unpaired
`CONTRA_REVENUE` leg is rejected as an attempted write-off (all `400
MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT_NOT_ALLOWED`). A `reason_code` is mandatory (AC #14). The
preparer actor is the AUTHENTICATED subject (stamped server-side, never read from
the body); the approver is assigned by the dual-control approval flow. A
governed adjustment whose gross (`Σ DR`) crosses the tenant's D2 threshold routes
to dual-control (`409 DUAL_CONTROL_REQUIRED`) instead of posting inline.

The governed action wire token (`"ROUNDING_CORRECTION"` /
`"SUSPENSE_CLEAR"`) — selects the allow-list, parsed in `into_domain`.

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency of the adjustment (every leg shares it).

The payer tenant the legs attribute to when the adjustment touches a
payer-scoped balance (`AR` / `UNALLOCATED`); `null` for a payer-less internal
clean-up.

reason_code.description: The mandatory business reason code (AC #14); an empty/blank one is rejected.

tax.description:
The authoritative tax breakdown for a tax-bearing action (never recomputed);
usually empty for the MVP actions.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this posts into; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

The `POST /manual-adjustments` response: a reference to the governed
adjustment's posting. A fresh post renders `201`, an idempotent replay `200`
(the handler reads `replayed`). Mirrors [`CreditNoteResponse`].

+ `side` carry the stable wire literals (parsed at [`ManualAdjustmentRequest::into_domain`]):
the class is an [`AccountClass`] token (e.g. `"SUSPENSE"`, `"CASH_CLEARING"`,
`"AR"`, `"GOODWILL"`); the side is `"DR"` / `"CR"` ([`Side`]). A leg outside the
action's code-owned allow-list — or any `REVENUE` / `CONTRACT_LIABILITY` leg, or
an unpaired `CONTRA_REVENUE` write-off — is rejected by the domain `govern` gate
(`400 MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT_NOT_ALLOWED`). `revenue_stream` is carried only for a
per-stream class and is otherwise `null`.

The leg amount in minor units (`> 0`; the domain `govern` rejects
zero/negative legs).

a point-in-time item produces none.

reflection of the validated token context — AM performs no
tenant-existence check here. `subject_type` is the optional `IdP` claim
and is omitted from the wire when absent rather than serialised as

post)` PEP gate authorizes it.

correlation_id.description:
Caller-supplied trace token propagated onto the entry (NOT an authority
claim — the poster identity is the authenticated subject, stamped
server-side, never read from the body).

due_date.description:
AR due date stamped on the AR line (drives AR-aging); `None` ⇒ due on
posting.

period_id.description: The fiscal `period_id` (`YYYYMM`) the entry posts into.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this posts into (= `entry.tenant_id`);
the PEP gate target. Carried in the body, not the path.

PostInvoiceResponseDto.description:
The `POST /journal-entries` (invoice-post) response: the posted-entry
reference (`entry_id`, `created_seq`, `replayed`) plus the recognition
schedules materialized in the SAME transaction (`schedules`, empty when the
invoice carried no deferred items). Extends the bare posting reference with
the discovery half of the recognition-schedule surface — the minted
`schedule_id`s are otherwise only observable on the event bus. On an
idempotent replay (`replayed = true`) the schedules are those the original
post materialized.

PostingPolicyResponse.description:
The written posting-policy version (the minted `version` + the values it
carries; the resolver picks the latest `effective_from`).

effective_from.description: The instant this version takes effect.

version.description: The minted version (`max + 1`, `0` for the first).

PostingPolicyView.description:
The tenant's effective posting policy (read-surface) — the configured version
in force, or the gear defaults when the tenant has set none.

PostingRefDto.description:
Reference to a posted (or idempotently replayed) entry. `replayed` is `true`
when the call matched a prior post (the handler then renders `200`, not
`201`).

Predicate.description: A predicate comparing a resource property to a value or subquery.

oneOf.description: Equality: `resource_property = value`
Set membership: `resource_property IN (values)`

allOf.description: Group membership: `resource_property IN (SELECT resource_id FROM membership WHERE group_id IN (group_ids))`

oneOf.description: Group membership: `resource_property IN (SELECT resource_id FROM membership WHERE group_id IN (group_ids))`

allOf.description: Group subtree: `resource_property IN (SELECT resource_id FROM membership WHERE group_id IN (SELECT descendant_id FROM closure WHERE ancestor_id IN (ancestor_ids)))`

oneOf.description: Group subtree: `resource_property IN (SELECT resource_id FROM membership WHERE group_id IN (SELECT descendant_id FROM closure WHERE ancestor_id IN (ancestor_ids)))`

allOf.description: Tenant subtree: `resource_property IN (SELECT descendant_id FROM tenant_closure WHERE ancestor_id = root_tenant_id)`

oneOf.description: Tenant subtree: `resource_property IN (SELECT descendant_id FROM tenant_closure WHERE ancestor_id = root_tenant_id)`

archived_at.description:
When the book was archived (D-522); null while it is not. The book list hides it unless
asked `archived eq true`; a read by id, the export and the consumer reads ignore the mark.

archived_by.description: Who archived it; null while it is not archived.

archived_by_name.description:
The current name of `archived_by` (D-519); null when no name is available now, and on a
write answer.

description.description: Free text, at most 2000 characters, or `null` (D-444).
Omitted keeps the description, `null` clears it; at most 2000 characters (D-444).

PricingApprovalKind.description:
A kind of approval unit pricing records (spec §6). No CHECK holds the stored column: the
repository reads it through this set, so a unit of another kind is a corrupt row (500).

PricingApprovalUnitCounts.description:
`GET /approval-units/counts` (D-470): the units the list's narrowing keeps, by state and by
kind, every state and kind named (0 when none), and their total.

PricingApprovalUnitDto.description:
An approval unit with its snapshot, decisions and, on the card, the live impact; and whether
its reader may approve it (D-471).

caller_can_approve.description:
Whether the caller may Approve this unit now (D-471): the approval engine's own rule
(`bss_approval::approve_eligibility`, D-459) over the unit's stored items and its decisions,
with the caller as the voter. It is false for a decided unit, for its submitter and every
author of its items (separation of duties) and for a caller who already voted in its current
generation. It means Approve only: a reject judges no separation of duties. It also
requires the caller's `approval_unit:approve` grant on this unit (D-497). Without that
grant the vote door is 403.

caller_can_reject.description:
Whether the caller may reject this unit now (D-497): the approve grant, the unit pending,
and no vote by the caller in this generation.

caller_can_withdraw.description:
Whether the caller may withdraw this unit now (D-497): the caller submitted it, the unit
is pending, and the caller holds the submit grant the withdraw door asks.

kind.description:
The unit's kind, one pricing records: a stored unit of another kind is a corrupt row (500),
never served.

submit_note.description:
The submitter's note (D-445), the unit shape products shares (P-D-219): the note a plan
revision's submit or publish-changes sent (D-464), or null. A single price's submit takes
none.

submitted_by_name.description:
The current name of `submitted_by` (D-519): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

PricingApprovalUnitKindCounts.description: The units of each kind pricing records (D-470).

PricingApprovalUnitList.description:
One page of the unit list (D-458): its units, and the toolkit pager's `page_info`, whose
`next_cursor` continues it.

PricingBillingTiming.description: When a charge is billed: in advance of its period or in arrears.

PricingBookIdentity.description:
A book named beside its id (D-516): id, code, name and currency. Validity stays on
[`PricingPlanBook`].

PricingBookPriceCounts.description:
A book's prices by state — a rejected price included — and its approved prices by where their
window stands today: `approved` = `scheduled + active + superseded` (D-441).

PricingChangeKind.description: What a price row asks the prices unit to do (D-520, D-521). `set` is a price.

PricingDecisionDto.description: One reviewer decision; decisions of earlier generations are kept and marked stale.

actor_name.description:
The current name of `actor` (D-519): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

PricingDimensionEntry.description: One key of `PUT /dimension-keys`: the key and its whole list of values (a full replace).

PricingDimensionKey.description: One key of the registry as the reads and writes answer it.

PricingDimensionKeyPatch.description:
`PATCH /dimension-keys` (D-436): the values of ONE declared key to add and to remove; keys
themselves are added and removed by the PUT.

PricingDimensionRegistry.description: The registry as `GET`, `PUT` and `PATCH /dimension-keys` answer it (D-436).

PricingDimensionValue.description: One value of a key with its use.

PricingDimensionValueUsage.description:
What uses one dimension value (D-436): the prices, of any state, whose entry names the key
and whose chain is the value. A value with prices is not removed (`DIM_VALUE_IN_USE`).

PricingEffectivePolicyDto.description: `GET /approval-policy/{kind}/effective` (D-481): the quorum a submit of `kind` needs now.

PricingEligibility.description: Who may take a price: every subscription, or new ones only.

PricingEntryPriceCounts.description:
An entry's prices by state; a rejected price is not counted (D-428). The approved ones are
also counted by where their window stands on the day of the read (D-440): today, or the
`as_of` of the book's entries list (D-473). `approved` = `scheduled + active + superseded`.

active.description: Approved prices in force on the day.

scheduled.description: Approved prices that start after the day.

superseded.description: Approved prices whose window ended on or before the day.

PricingEntryPriceList.description:
`GET /price-book-entries/{id}/prices` (D-440): every price of the entry in every state, the
default chain first, then each dimension value's chain in ascending order; each chain by
`effective_from`, then `version_no`.

PricingEntryReferenceState.description:
Where an entry's SKU reference stands with Products; `released` once its book is archived
(D-522).

PricingEntryUsage.description:
An entry's usage (D-428): its prices by state; `plans`, the distinct plans with a draft,
pending, scheduled or published revision whose items name it; `plans_superseded_only`, the
distinct plans that name it only through superseded revisions (they still keep it
`ENTRY_IN_USE`).

PricingItemReferenceState.description: Where a plan item's SKU reference stands with Products.

PricingModel.description: An entry's model (D-427), the model of every price of the entry.

PricingPeriod.description: A recurring entry's period; a usage or one-time entry has none.

PricingPinnedPriceDto.description:
`GET /prices/{id}`: one approved price as stored, served forever whatever its window (D-422),
with its entry's SKU, charge kind and period and its book's currency, or a cancelled one
(D-520). Stored facts only: no value computed from today, and no authoring internals.

approved_by_unit_id.description: The approval unit that applied the price.

closed_explicitly.description: The window was ended explicitly rather than by a successor's start.

dim_value.description: The value's chain; null for the default chain.

keep_for_bound.description: The price is kept for pinned subscriptions (the predecessor of a `new` price).

paired_price_id.description: A temporary price's return partner, or the price a return partner restores.

price.description: The price's money as stored, amounts as exact decimal text.

oneOf.description:
`cancelled` for a price cancelled before it started, the entry list's token (D-520): a
stored fact, the same on every day. Absent on an approved price, whose display status
depends on the day, which this read never computes (D-422). Its own one-value set, so the
schema offers nothing the read never serves.

version_no.description: The price's place in its entry's order of prices.

PricingPinnedPriceStatus.description:
A pinned price's status (D-520): `cancelled` for a price cancelled before it started, the
token the entry's price list shows. The only status `GET /prices/{id}` serves.

PricingPlanApprovalProgress.description:
A pending revision's vote progress (D-462), counts only: its unit, the approve votes the quorum
counts (the current generation's, not stale: the approval library's `counted_approvals`, the
count the vote door judges by) and the quorum.

PricingPlanBook.description: The book a plan's current revision prices on (D-485, D-515).

valid_from.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, or null when the book is open on that side.

valid_until.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, exclusive, or null when the book is open on that side.

PricingPlanChange.description:
How a plan's list row is changing (D-485): a draft or pending revision, a scheduled one
still waiting for its date, or none.

PricingPlanChangeCounts.description: Every change the list can name, 0 when none.

PricingPlanCheckBlockingPrice.description: A pending price that blocks a check row (D-466): its approval unit, the price and its entry.

PricingPlanCheckDto.description: One row of a revision's checks (D-408). An `info` row is always ok and never blocks.

blocked_by.description:
The approval units whose pending prices would cover what is uncovered: computed on every
read, never stored (spec §6).

blocked_by_prices.description:
The pending prices behind `blocked_by`, one per price, ordered by unit then price (D-466):
the units they name are exactly `blocked_by`.

subjects.description:
The items that turn the row red, in the revision's item order (D-466): empty for a green
row and for a plan-wide one (the plan's name, its book, the book's validity, the item
count, and the information rows).

PricingPlanCheckSubject.description: An item a check row is about (D-466): the item, its SKU and the entry it names.

price_book_entry_id.description: Null for an item that names no entry.

PricingPlanChecksDto.description: `GET /plan-revisions/{id}/checks`: every check on the sale date, from fresh SKU reads.

quorum_required.description:
The `plan_revision` quorum a submit of this revision needs (D-481): the tenant's effective
policy, the number the APPROVAL info row already shows. The revision itself has no quorum.

ready.description: Every check is ok: the revision may be submitted.

sale_date.description: `available_from`, or today for a revision sold from its publication.

PricingPlanClone.description:
`POST /plans/{id}/clone`: the new plan's own code and name; its draft rev 1 copies the source's
published revision, and its sale date unless the body names one (D-463).

available_from.description:
Rev 1's sale date, `YYYY-MM-DD` (D-463): omitted keeps the source's, a date overrides it,
null clears it ("at publish"). A malformed date is 400 `DATE_INVALID`.

code.description: The new plan's code, under the rule of `POST /plans` (D-468).

PricingPlanCounts.description: `GET /plans/counts` (D-485): every plan the list's narrowing keeps, by the derived axes.

PricingPlanCreate.description: `POST /plans`: a plan and its draft rev 1 on `book_id`.

available_from.description:
Rev 1's sale date, `YYYY-MM-DD` (D-463); omitted or null means "at publish". A malformed
date is 400 `DATE_INVALID`, as the revision PATCH answers it.

code.description:
1 to 32 characters of `A-Z`, `0-9`, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter or a digit, judged as
sent (D-468): blank is 400 `PLAN_CODE_REQUIRED`, any other code off the rule 400
`PLAN_CODE_INVALID`, and a code over 64 characters 400 `FIELD_TOO_LONG` (D-457).

PricingPlanCurrent.description:
A plan's current revision as its list row names it (D-460): the draft or pending one, else
the scheduled one, else the published one in effect, chosen over the states the revisions read
today (D-447).

book.description: The book it prices on (D-485, D-515): that book's id, code, name, currency and validity.

created_by.description: Its author, who edits it while it is a draft (D-404); not the plan's.

created_by_name.description:
The current name of `created_by` (D-519): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.
