item_count.description: How many items it holds, every item counted (a legacy one without an entry too, D-467).

sku_ids.description:
The SKUs of its items, one per item, in ascending order. They may differ from the plans
`GET /plans?sku_id=` keeps, which need an item with an entry and read the stored state
(D-434).

state.description: The state it reads today (D-447): `draft`, `pending`, `scheduled` or `published`.

PricingPlanDto.description: A plan with the headers of its revisions in revision order.

change.description: The change on that day: `draft`, `pending`, `scheduled` or `none` (D-484).

created_by_name.description:
The current name of `created_by` (D-519): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

oneOf.description:
The revision being changed or waiting, else the one in effect (D-460); null without
revisions.
The published revision in effect today (D-460); null before the first publication.

last_activity_at.description:
The latest `updated_at` of the plan and its revisions (D-484). A page ordered by it carries
the same instant. Not the If-Match clock (`updated_at`).

published_rev.description:
The revision number the plan sells today (D-447): the last one published, or the number of
a scheduled revision whose date has come, before its switch is persisted. It never counts
a revision that is still waiting for its date.

selling.description: Whether the plan sells on the request's day (D-484). Never null.

PricingPlanEntrySummary.description:
One distinct entry a revision's items name, with the default chain's price in force on the
revision's sale date (D-480).

oneOf.description:
The default chain's approved price in force on the revision's sale date, chosen by
`price_book_entries::headline` (D-440, D-472). Null when only value chains price the
entry, when none is in force, or when the caller's `price_book` read does not admit the
entry's book (D-434).

PricingPlanInEffect.description: The revision a plan sells today (D-460): its published revision in effect (D-447).

sku_ids.description:
The SKUs of that revision's items, one per item, in ascending order (D-480). The same set
a draft or pending revision reports as `carried_sku_ids`.

PricingPlanItemCreate.description:
`POST /plan-revisions/{id}/items`: one item, one op with its own key (D-407). A plan item is a
SKU and, once the author has chosen it, its entry in the plan's book (D-467, D-512). The entry
may be absent: the draft holds the SKU and a later PATCH sets the entry. Submit still needs an
entry for every item. `treatment`, `included_qty` and `qty_min` are refused (400
`BODY_UNEXPECTED`).

price_book_entry_id.description:
The entry of the plan's book that prices the SKU. Absent or null adds an entry-less item
(D-512). A given entry is still judged: another book, another SKU, or an unknown entry.

created_by_name.description:
The current name of `created_by` (D-519): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

price_book_entry_id.description:
The entry that prices the item. Null while a draft item waits for its entry (D-512), and
for a legacy item stored without one (D-467).

reservation_id.description: None until a reserve answers: a copied item attaches after its write (D-413).

PricingPlanItemPatch.description:
`PATCH /plan-items/{id}`, draft only: never a SKU change (the SKU is the item's reference).
It sets the item's entry (D-467, D-512), including on an item that has none. `treatment`,
`included_qty` and `qty_min` are refused (400 `BODY_UNEXPECTED`). A null entry is 400
`ITEM_ENTRY_MISSING`: a PATCH never clears an entry.

state.description:
The revision's state as it reads today (D-447): a scheduled revision whose date has come
reads `published`, and the one it replaces `superseded`, before the switch is persisted.

PricingPlanItemReadDto.description: `GET /plan-items/{id}` (D-434): the item with its revision's number and state and its plan.

page_info.description: The toolkit pager's page (D-485). `limit` is the page size, 500 by default and at most 500.

PricingPlanReservationItemDto.description: One item on the reservations read (D-480).

PricingPlanReservationsDto.description:
`GET /plan-revisions/{id}/reservations` (D-480): each item's reference, and whether they have
all settled.

settled.description: The same rule as the revision's `reservations_settled`: `lost` counts as settled.

PricingPlanRevisionDto.description: A revision with its items (D-407: items are a sub-resource, read with their revision).

oneOf.description:
The vote progress of a pending revision (D-462), readable under plan read; null for any
other state.

approved_at.description: When it was approved (D-461): the decision of the unit that approved it; null before.

available_from.description: The sale date; null means "at publish".

created_by.description: The draft's author: the one principal who edits it and its items (D-404).

created_by_name.description:
The current name of `created_by` (D-519): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

published_at.description:
When it took effect (D-447): its approval's instant, or 00:00 UTC of its sale date for a
revision that waited for it; null until then.

reservations_settled.description:
True when no item is `unreserved` or `confirmation_pending` (D-480). `lost` counts as
settled, so settled is not a green check. Computed from the items in hand, on every answer.

state.description: The state as it reads today (D-447); `scheduled` is approved and waiting for its sale date.

submitted_at.description:
When it was submitted for approval (D-461): the submission of its pending unit, or of the
unit that approved it; null for a draft.

PricingPlanRevisionHeader.description: One revision of a plan as its plan lists it: the header, without items.

approved_at.description:
When it was approved (D-461): the decision of the unit that approved it, which a scheduled
revision needs because its `published_at` is null until its date; null before.

created_by.description: Its author (D-461): the one principal who edits it while it is a draft (D-404).

created_by_name.description:
The current name of `created_by` (D-519): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

published_at.description:
When it took effect: its approval's instant, or 00:00 UTC of its sale date for a revision
that waited for it (D-447, D-450); null until then.

state.description: The state as it reads today (D-447).

submitted_at.description:
When it was submitted for approval (D-461): the submission of its pending unit, or of the
unit that approved it; null for a draft, also one back from a reject, a withdraw or an
unschedule.

PricingPlanRevisionPatch.description:
`PATCH /plan-revisions/{id}`, draft only: the book and the sale date, never an item list
(D-407). A book change remaps each item to the new book's entry of the same (SKU, charge kind,
period, model, policy digest) and equal dimension key (D-502); an unmatched item keeps its
entry and the checks show it foreign.

carried_sku_ids.description:
Draft or pending only (null otherwise): the SKU ids of the plan's published revision in
effect today (D-447), `[]` when none is in effect. The set a re-add of a deprecated SKU
judges (D-465).

entries.description: One per distinct entry the items name, in entry id order.

sale_date.description:
The checks' sale date (`domain::plan::sale_date`): `available_from`, or today for "at
publish". A past `available_from` answers that past date, as the checks do.

PricingPlanRevisionReadDto.description:
`GET /plan-revisions/{id}` (D-480): the revision, its sale date, one summary per distinct
entry its items name, and, while it is draft or pending, the SKUs the plan sells today.
Write answers keep [`PricingPlanRevisionDto`].

PricingPlanRevisionSubmitReceipt.description:
The `plan_revision` unit a submission recorded and the revision after the transaction:
pending under the unit, or published when quorum zero applied it at once.

PricingPlanRevisionSubmitRequest.description:
`POST /plan-revisions/{id}/submit`: an optional body with the submitter's note (D-464). No
body, `{}` and `note: null` carry none; any other key is 400 `BODY_UNEXPECTED`.

note.description:
The submitter's note for the approver, stored on the unit as `submit_note`; at most 2000
characters (400 `NOTE_TOO_LONG`).

PricingPlanSellingCounts.description: `selling` is never null, so the two buckets add up to `total`.

model.description:
Required and fixed for the entry's life (D-427): `flat`, `per_unit`, `graduated`,
`volume` or `package`, one the SKU's charge kind allows.

oneOf.description:
Required for usage entries; immutable after creation. Identity is server assigned.
`quantity_semantics.fold`, `reset` and `partial_window` may be absent or null; the server
fills `SUM`, `rating_window_start` and `actual_quantity_full_thresholds` (D-513).

model.description: The entry's model (D-427), fixed for its life and part of its key.

oneOf.description: Immutable policy materialized from the entry; null for legacy/non-usage entries.

usage_sku_version.description:
The SKU head's `published_version` when the meter was checked. Null for a non-usage entry
and for a usage entry written before D-514.

PricingPriceBookEntryList.description: One page of a book's entries (D-483), ordered `(sku_id, charge_kind, model, id)`.

page_info.description:
`limit` is the page size (500 by default and at most); `next_cursor` continues the page and
carries the list's `$filter` and day.

PricingPriceBookEntryReadDto.description:
What the two entry reads answer (D-428): the entry's fields, its `usage`, its `current_price`
(D-440): the default chain's approved price in force on the day, as D-434 chooses and shows it
— and its `next_price` (D-472): the default chain's earliest scheduled price, else its newest
draft or pending price (the highest `version_no`, then the latest `created_at`). Each is `null`
when there is none, or when the caller does not hold `price_book` read on the entry's book.
The day is today, or the `as_of` of the book's entries list (D-473).
Every other answer that carries an entry (POST, PATCH, the stored receipt, the export,
publish-changes) keeps [`PricingPriceBookEntryDto`].

PricingPriceBookReadDto.description:
What the two book reads answer (D-441): the book's fields and its `stats`. The write answers
(POST, PATCH, the stored receipt), the export and publish-changes keep [`PriceBookDto`].

PricingPriceBookStats.description:
A book's stats (D-441): its entries and their distinct SKUs; the distinct plans with a draft,
pending, scheduled or published revision on the book (`plans`), and those that name it only
through superseded revisions (`plans_superseded_only`, what the delete refuses as
`BOOK_IN_PLAN_HISTORY`); its prices by state; its `prices` units in review; and the latest
change of the book, its entries, their prices and its units. `DELETE /price-books/{id}`
succeeds exactly when `entries`, `plans` and `plans_superseded_only` are 0 (D-444).

released_entries.description:
The entries still `released` when the answer is built; null when they could not be read
after the unarchive committed (the book's entry list says which).

PricingPriceBookUnarchiveDto.description:
`POST /price-books/{id}/unarchive` (D-522): the book, listed again, and the entries still
`released` after the door drove their re-reservations: their SKU refused a new reservation
(retired, say), or Products has not answered yet. Each stays read-only until it is re-reserved.

price.description: Money in the entry's model (D-427); a price carries no model of its own.

PricingPriceCreated.description: The draft price, and its return partner when the request made a temporary pair.

cancelled_by_unit_id.description: The unit that cancelled this price, when `state` is `cancelled` (D-520).

change_kind.description:
`set` for a price; `cancel` or `end` for a row that asks to cancel or end the approved
price `target_price_id` names (D-520, D-521). Such a row carries that price's money
unchanged and is never a price in force.

created_by_name.description:
The current name of `created_by` (D-519): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

model.description: The entry's model, read-only (D-427): a price has no model of its own.

status.description:
Display state of matrix row 10: an approved price shows where its window stands today.
A cancelled price shows `cancelled` (D-520). A `cancel` or `end` row shows its state, and
`superseded` once applied (D-520, D-521).

target_price_id.description: The approved price a `cancel` or `end` row names; null on a `set` row.

effective_to.description:
The new end, `YYYY-MM-DD`, exclusive: after today, after the price's start, and no later
than its current end.

effective_from.description: A temporary draft's start moves with its end; a return's start is its pair's end.

temporary_until.description:
The end of the temporary half of a draft; its pair is re-derived over the new dates. Any
other price, and `null`, is 400 `TEMPORARY_PRICE_FIXED`.

PricingPriceStatus.description:
A price's display state (matrix row 10): an approved price shows where its window stands.
A cancelled price shows `cancelled` (D-520).

PricingProposedPrice.description:
One draft price as the operator sees it before publishing: the entry key, the chain,
the approved predecessor it follows, its pair partner and the default selection.

impact.description:
Prices and entries the listed drafts touch, the plan revisions naming those entries, and
subscriptions (unavailable until the Subscriptions integration).

note.description:
The submitter's note for the approver (D-464), stored on the unit as `submit_note`; at most
2000 characters (400 `NOTE_TOO_LONG`). Omitted or null, none.

oneOf.description:
Why the op releases its reference: `book_archived` for a `release` (D-522); null for every
other op.

ref_kind.description: The reference the op works for (D-407).

PricingReferenceOpKind.description: What a reference op does (D-413); `release` lets an archived book's entry go (D-522).

PricingReferenceOpReason.description: Why a reference op releases its reference (D-522): its entry's book was archived.

PricingReferenceOpRefKind.description: The reference a reference op works for (D-407).

PricingResolveBindingDto.description: The price bound for the period, as stored.

dim_used.description: The chain the bound price belongs to: the value, or null for the default chain.

effective_to.description:
The stored window's end, for information: a successor's start sets it, including a `new`
successor a pinned subscription does not take, so it is not an end for the binding.

keep_for_bound.description: The price is kept for pinned subscriptions (the predecessor of a `new` price).

pinned_from.description: The pin the renewal walk started from; null for a signup.

price.description: The price's money as stored, in the item's model (D-427), amounts as exact decimal text.

PricingResolveChainDto.description: One row of an item's matrix: the default chain (`dim_value` null) or one value.

uncovered.description:
Neither the value's own chain nor the default binds on the date: `binding` is null. Never
a refusal and never an invented price.

PricingResolveDto.description:
`GET /resolve`: one plan revision resolved on one date with the caller's pins (D-419). It
carries no totals and no promotion (D-409, D-415).

currency_minor_digits.description: The currency's scale: the number of minor digits money carries.

items.description: Every item of the revision, or the one `item_id` names.

rounding_policy.description:
The tenant's `default_rounding`, as stored: a string, since no CHECK guards the column
(D-437, D-439).

state.description:
The revision's state as it reads today (D-447): `published`, `superseded`, or `scheduled`
for a revision asked on or after its sale date while that date has not come yet (D-454). No
other revision resolves.

PricingResolveInputDto.description: A resolved invoice input and where it came from; both null when no source holds it.

PricingResolveItemDto.description:
One item of the revision on the date: its SKU and entry (D-467), its SKU version and resolved
invoice inputs (D-421), and its chain matrix (D-420).

billing_timing.description: The SKU version's, else the tenant `default_timing` (PRD AC #13).

chains.description:
The default chain, then each value registered today in the registry's order, then any
other value a pin names.

oneOf.description: Null without an entry.

gl_code.description: The SKU version's, else the tenant `default_gl`.

invoice_line_template.description:
The entry's override, else the SKU version's template, else the tenant template for the
charge kind.

meter.description: The meter of that SKU version; both null without a version.

oneOf.description: The entry's model (D-427), the model of every binding's money; null without an entry.

price_book_entry_id.description: Null for a legacy item stored without an entry (D-467), which has no chains.

oneOf.description:
The SKU version in force on the date; null when Products has no version on that date or
does not know the SKU.

tax_category.description: The SKU version's, else the tenant `default_tax_category`.

oneOf.description: Immutable policy projected from the selected entry; null for legacy entries.

PricingResolveMeterDto.description: The meter of the SKU version in force on the date.

PricingResolveSkuVersionDto.description: The SKU version an item reads on the date.

PricingResolveSource.description: Where a resolved invoice input came from (D-421).

PricingResolvedRevisionState.description:
The state of a revision that resolves, as it reads today (D-447): a published or
superseded one on every date (D-419), a scheduled one from its sale date on (D-454). No
other resolves.

PricingRevisionChecksBatchDto.description:
`GET /plan-revisions/checks` (D-482): the checks of the revisions the caller may read, and
the ids the tenant does not hold or the plan-read scope does not admit.

PricingRevisionChecksDto.description: `GET /plan-revisions/checks` (D-482): one revision's checks, the single read's answer.

currencies.description: The currencies a new book may take; empty means any (D-438).

default_rounding.description:
One of the five modes (D-437) once written through the door; a string, not an enum: no
CHECK guards the column, and a legacy value reads back as stored (D-439).

updated_at.description: When the settings were last written; null before the first write (version 0).

updated_by.description: Who wrote them last; null before the first write and on a row written before D-438.

updated_by_name.description:
The current name of `updated_by` (D-519): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when `updated_by` is null, when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

currencies.description: Required (D-438): the currencies a NEW book may take, a full replace; `[]` is any.

updated_by_name.description:
Ignored (D-519): the writer's name that `GET /settings` shows. It is accepted so that a
read's body without `version`, `updated_at` and `updated_by` stays a PUT body (D-438).

changing.description: A draft or a pending price exists (D-486).

status.description:
`priced` when an approved price is in force today, else `scheduled` when one starts
later, else `unpriced` (D-486).

PricingSkuEntryDto.description:
One entry of a SKU as `GET /price-book-entries?sku_id=` answers it (D-434, D-486): the entry,
its book's code, name and currency, its usage (D-428), its `status` and `changing` on today,
the default chain's price in force today (`current_price`) and its `next_price` (D-472),
chosen as the entry reads choose it (the highest `version_no` orders the drafts and pending
prices). Each price is `null` when there is none, or when the caller does not hold
`price_book` read (the export's grant). `status` and `changing` are not money.

PricingSkuEntryList.description: `GET /price-book-entries?sku_id=` (D-486): one page of the SKU's entries.

page_info.description: `limit` is the page size. `next_cursor` continues the page.

PricingSkuEntryStatus.description:
Where a SKU's entry stands today (D-486): an approved price in force, else one that
starts later, else neither. Not a price's display status.

PricingSubmitReceipt.description: The unit a submission recorded and its prices after the transaction.

PricingVoteOutcome.description: What a vote did: counted toward the quorum, or applied, rejected or withdrew the unit.

PricingVoteRequest.description: A vote names the generation its reviewer saw; a reject needs a note.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem+json. `context` varies by error category.

ProductsApprovalKind.description:
A kind of approval unit products records (P-D-227). No CHECK holds the stored column: the
repository reads it through this set, so a unit of another kind is a corrupt row (500).

ProductsApprovalUnitCounts.description:
`GET /approval-units/counts` (P-D-227): the units the list's narrowing keeps, by state and by
kind, every state and kind named (0 when none), and their total.

ProductsApprovalUnitKindCounts.description: The units of each kind products records (P-D-227).

ProductsBillingTiming.description: When a SKU's charge is billed: in advance of its period or in arrears.

ProductsCategoryDto.description: Wire representation of the registry Category.

archived_at.description:
When the retired category was archived (P-D-263); null while it is not. Its list hides it
unless asked `archived eq true`; a read by id ignores the mark.

archived_by.description: Who archived it; null while it is not archived.

archived_by_name.description:
The current name of `archived_by` (P-D-262), as `created_by_name` names its actor; null
when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

ProductsCategoryItem.description:
A category as its reads answer it (P-D-215): the category's fields and `sku_count`, the SKUs
that are not retired naming it — the ones that keep it in use (P-D-208), so a category with
`sku_count` 0 may be retired.

ProductsDerivedDeclaration.description:
A derived usage type's declaration (P-D-229, P-D-230): its inputs, the formula applied to one
granule's folded inputs, and the output's unit, scale and rounding.

ProductsDerivedInput.description: One input of a derived usage type: a raw GTS usage type, folded over one granule.

max_hold_seconds.description: Required for `time_weighted` (1 to 86 400 seconds) and refused otherwise; absent when none.

usage_type_ref.description: A GTS usage type id; never a `products.derived/` id.

ProductsDerivedMeterRef.description: What a pricing usage policy names as its meter (O-2, H1).

ProductsDerivedUsageType.description: A derived usage type with its versions' headers, oldest first.

created_by_name.description:
The current name of `created_by` (P-D-262): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

ProductsDerivedUsageTypeItem.description: A derived usage type as the list pages it.

created_by_name.description:
The current name of `created_by` (P-D-262): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

latest.description: The latest version, in the version-read shape (P-D-257).

latest_version.description: The highest version number. Kept beside [`Self::latest`] (P-D-257).

ProductsDerivedUsageTypeRequest.description: `POST /derived-usage-types`: a new type and its version 1.

ProductsDerivedUsageTypeVersion.description: One version of a derived usage type, with what a pricing author copies into a usage policy.

created_by_name.description:
The current name of `created_by` (P-D-262): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

digest.description: The stored SHA-256 of the declaration's canonical bytes, 64 lowercase hex digits.

ProductsDerivedVersionHeader.description: A version as the type read lists it.

created_by_name.description:
The current name of `created_by` (P-D-262): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

ProductsLifecycle.description: A SKU's lifecycle. A retire under review is `retire_pending`, not a lifecycle (P-D-248).

ProductsReferenceKind.description: The kind of owner object a SKU reference protects.

ProductsReferenceState.description: A SKU reference's state; a released one is a tombstone.

ProductsSkuCounts.description:
The SKU list's tab counts (P-D-211): every SKU the narrowing keeps, those in each lifecycle,
and those a pending approval unit locks (in any lifecycle), none of them archived; and the
archived SKUs the narrowing keeps, which no other number counts (P-D-263).

ProductsSkuHistoryEntry.description:
One act in a SKU's history (P-D-213): when (`at`, the row's `written_at`: the submit, change and
draft doors take it before their transaction and keep it across a retry, the other writers inside
the attempt — never the commit; the history is in the order the acts wrote, by the audit row's id), who (`actor`, the nil uuid for the system's orphan-fence expiry), what
(`action`), the lifecycle it found and left (`null` on a row written before the audit log
carried them, on a create's `from`), the approval unit it concerned and its kind, and the note
it carried (a change's note, a decision's note, or the expiry's TTL).

action.description: The audit row's action: a string, since no CHECK holds the column to a set (P-D-217).

actor_name.description:
The current name of `actor` (P-D-262): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now.

ProductsSkuSubmitRequest.description:
The optional body of `POST /skus/{id}/submit` and `/retire` (P-D-219): the submitter's note,
at most 2000 characters (400 `NOTE_TOO_LONG`), stored on the unit as `submit_note` and on the
submit's history row, as sent. No body, `{}` and `note: null` carry none; any other field is a
400.

ProductsUsageTypeDto.description:
One usage type as the picker offers it. Prefixed: the usage collector's own `UsageTypeDto` is
in the same served document.

ProductsUsageTypeList.description:
A page of the picker, with the catalog's provenance (`registry`, `usage_collector`,
`local_dev_static`).

ProductsUsageTypePageInfo.description: The page's cursors and the size the catalog actually applied.

ProductsVoteOutcome.description: What a vote did: counted toward the quorum, or applied, rejected or withdrew the unit.

ProvenanceDto.description: Who admitted the current revision and how. Selected as one group.

compat_forced.description: Whether ADR-0004 `force` waived a cross-minor check; `null` for Instances.

ProvisioningRequestDto.description:
The provisioning request body: the target seller tenant, accounts, currency
scales, and the fiscal-calendar config to seed in one transaction. The
tenant is carried in the **body** (not the path) — the gear's REST surface is
tenant-from-context/body per the vhp-core convention (RBAC/RMS), and a
provision targets a seller the caller authorizes via the PEP gate.

ProvisioningResultDto.description:
The provisioning result: the accounts THIS call created + per-grain
created-vs-existing counts.

PspSettlementReportRequest.description:
`POST /ledger/control/psp-settlement-report` request body: the PSP's net settled
amount for `(tenant, period)`.

settled_minor.description: Net settled amount in minor units the PSP reports (net of refunds/returns).

tenant_id.description: The seller tenant whose ledger this feeds; the PEP gate target. In the body.

PullRefDto.description:
GitHub-shaped `head`/`base` of a pull request: the branch name plus the
commit it pointed at. Distinct from [`GitRefDto`], which is the
commit-only shape branches and tags use.

ref.description: Branch name, under GitHub's own key.

node_id.description: GitHub's GraphQL global id, as GitHub itself returns it.

oneOf.description:
Who opened it, who it is assigned to, who was asked to review, and
the labels it carries.

PullRequestFileDto.description: GitHub-shaped changed file of a pull request.

patch.description: The file's unified diff, as GitHub returns it on this endpoint.

PullRequestMarkerDto.description:
Marker object GitHub attaches to issues that are pull requests.

The braces are load-bearing: serde serializes a braced empty struct as
`{}` (GitHub's marker shape) but a unit struct as `null`.

PutAddressReq.description: REST DTO for creating/upserting an address

PutNamedSettingRequest.description: Body of `PUT /named-settings/{key}`: the value to store under the key.

PutTenantMetadataDto.description:
Request body for `PUT /tenants/{tenant_id}/metadata/{type_id}`.

The wire shape is the JSON payload to upsert, transmitted in-place
as `TenantMetadataValue` (`type: object, additionalProperties: true`
per `OpenAPI`). No metadata fields cross the request envelope -- the
chained `type_id` is the path parameter, not part of the body.

value.description:
GTS-schema-validated metadata payload. The service rejects
`null` (`DomainError::Validation`) before any state read.

QuantitySemanticsRequest.description:
Quantity semantics on author input. `fold` defaults to `SUM` when absent or null (D-513).
Deprecated: the deploy-3 copy is verified and dropped (D-514).

oneOf.description: Absent or null defaults to `SUM` (D-513).

QueryAggregatedUsageRecordsRequest.description:
Aggregated-query request body for
`POST /usage-collector/v1/records/aggregate`. The typed `gts_id`, the
`OData` `$filter`, and the `metadata.<key>` side-channel remain query
parameters (mirroring `GET /usage-collector/v1/records`); only the
aggregation spec (operator + group-by dimensions) ships in the body.

QuotaWarning.description: Per-tier, per-period quota warning entry in the SSE `done` event.

next_reset.description:
RFC 3339 timestamp of the next quota-period reset.
Present when `warning` or `exhausted` is true; absent otherwise.

RecognitionInputDto.description:
The optional per-item ASC 606 recognition spec on the wire (Slice 4). Maps to
the domain [`RecognitionInput`]; absence on an item ⇒ no deferral. `timing` is
`"point_in_time"` (no deferral, explicit) or `"straight_line"` (defer the
whole ex-tax amount over `periods` equal segments from `first_period_id`,
defaulted to the invoice period when omitted). The optional refs/flags carry
PO / SSP / VC / subscription context onto the materialized schedule.

first_period_id.description:
Straight-line only: first fiscal period (`YYYYMM`) the schedule recognizes
into; `None` ⇒ defaulted to the invoice period.

immaterial_one_shot_sku.description:
`true` iff the Catalog SKU is flagged immaterial-one-shot-eligible (an R4
exemption precondition). `None` ⇒ `false` (not eligible).

multi_po.description:
`true` for a genuine multi-performance-obligation line — the only case
where a missing/unresolvable SSP snapshot blocks the post (§4.4). `None` ⇒
`false` (single-PO).

periods.description:
Straight-line only: number of equal recognition segments (`>= 1`).
Required for `timing = "straight_line"`, ignored for `"point_in_time"`.

po_allocation_group.description: The PO / allocation group this line books under (audit, §4.7).

policy_ref.description: The deferral+timing policy version stamped immutably on the schedule.

ssp_snapshot_ref.description:
The SSP snapshot ref pinned at contract inception; required + resolvable
for a `multi_po` line (else `SSP_SNAPSHOT_REQUIRED`).

subscription_ref.description: The subscription/entitlement this obligation belongs to (audit).

vc_estimate_ref.description:
Variable-consideration estimate ref (carried only — VC posting is OUT of
the MVP, N-revrec-4).

vc_method_ref.description:
Variable-consideration method ref (carried only — VC posting is OUT of
the MVP, N-revrec-4).

RecognitionRunQueuedResponse.description:
The `POST /recognition-runs` response when the run had to park one or more
out-of-order segments `QUEUED` for a later drain (HTTP 202 Accepted): the run
ran (it may have released in-order segments) but a due segment's lower-period
predecessor was not yet `DONE` (§4.6). `status` is the fixed
`recognition-period-queued` token; `released` + `queued` are this pass's
tallies. A later run drains the `QUEUED` segments once their predecessors
commit. Mirrors `AllocationQueuedResponse`. The `Queued` arm of the outcome.

period_id.description: The period the run was triggered for (`YYYYMM`).

queued.description: Segments parked `QUEUED` this pass (a predecessor period was not `DONE`).

released.description: Segments released in order on this pass before/around the queued ones.

run_id.description: The run that executed (the queued ones are the out-of-order tail).

status.description: Always `recognition-period-queued` (a normal-body kebab-case token, not an error).

RecognitionRunResponse.description:
The `POST /recognition-runs` response when the run EXECUTED (fresh or an
idempotent replay of a prior trigger): the run identity + the release tally.
A fresh run renders `200`, an idempotent replay also `200` (the run already
committed under the original trigger; `replayed = true`). The `Ran` arm of
the outcome.

already_recognized.description: Segments that were already released (an idempotent `RECOGNITION` replay).

period_id.description: The period the run released for (`YYYYMM`).

released.description: Segments released on THIS pass (a fresh `DR CL / CR Revenue` post).

replayed.description:
`true` when this trigger replayed a prior run with the same
`(tenant, run_id)` (no new run row was inserted; no re-release).

run_id.description: The run that executed (minted by the trigger, or replayed).

RecognitionRunView.description:
The `GET /recognition-runs` / `GET /recognition-runs/{run_id}` response: one
recorded ASC 606 recognition run (read-surface R4). Drawn from the
`recognition_run` row (the `(tenant, period_id, run_id)` grain — the run is the
orchestration wrapper that released a period's due segments). `status` is the
run lifecycle (`RUNNING` ⇒ in-flight / `DONE` ⇒ completed / `FAILED` ⇒ aborted);
`started_at_utc` is when the run began. Tenant-scoped (SQL-level BOLA): an
unknown run — or one outside the caller's subtree — yields a `404` (no existence
leak). Mirrors [`DisputeView`].

period_id.description: The fiscal period (`YYYYMM`) the run released due segments for.

RecognitionScheduleListResponse.description:
The `GET /recognition-schedules` response: the recognition schedule headers
matching the `(tenant_id[, invoice_id][, revenue_stream])` filter (segments
omitted — the by-id surface carries those). A discovery surface for the
server-minted `schedule_id`; an empty list is a normal `200`, never a `404`.

truncated.description:
`true` when the result was capped server-side — more schedules exist than
returned (the list surface is not paginated). A client seeing `truncated`
must narrow the filter (`invoice_id` / `revenue_stream`) to see the rest.

RecognitionScheduleResponse.description:
The `GET /recognition-schedules/{schedule_id}` response: one schedule's
lifecycle view (design §3.7 / §4) — the schedule header (status, version,
revenue stream, currency, total-deferred / recognized-to-date, the originating
invoice + the §4.7 item-link anchor, the PO / subscription / policy refs) plus
its segments, ordered by `segment_no` (period order). A schedule outside the
caller's authorized subtree (or simply absent) yields a 404 — never this body
(no existence leak).

po_allocation_group.description: The PO / allocation group this obligation books under; `null` when none.

policy_ref.description: The immutable deferral/timing policy version stamped at build.

revenue_stream.description: The revenue stream the obligation books to (one schedule per stream).

segments.description: The schedule's segments, ordered by `segment_no` (period order).

source_invoice_item_ref.description:
The Contract-liability invoice line the schedule draws down (the §4.7
invoice-link anchor).

subscription_ref.description: The subscription / entitlement this obligation belongs to; `null` when none.

total_deferred_minor.description: The total deferred Contract-liability the schedule plans to release.

version.description: The lineage version (`0` fresh; `old + 1` for a `replace` successor).

RecognitionScheduleSegmentDto.description:
One recognition segment in the `GET /recognition-schedules/{schedule_id}`
response: the `segment_no` (immutable, 1:1 with `period_id`), the period it
recognizes into, its minor-unit amount, and its release status
(`PENDING` | `QUEUED` | `DONE`). A row of [`RecognitionScheduleResponse::segments`].

period_id.description: The fiscal period this segment recognizes into (`YYYYMM`).

RecognitionScheduleSummaryDto.description:
One recognition schedule header in the `GET /recognition-schedules` list
response — like [`RecognitionScheduleResponse`] but WITHOUT segments (the
by-id `GET /recognition-schedules/{schedule_id}` carries those). Maps from
[`bss_ledger_sdk::RecognitionScheduleSummaryView`].

po_allocation_group.description: The PO / allocation group this obligation books under; `null` when none.

policy_ref.description: The immutable deferral/timing policy version stamped at build.

revenue_stream.description: The revenue stream the obligation books to (one schedule per stream).

source_invoice_item_ref.description: The Contract-liability invoice line the schedule draws down.

subscription_ref.description: The subscription / entitlement this obligation belongs to; `null` when none.

total_deferred_minor.description: The total deferred Contract-liability the schedule plans to release.

version.description: The lineage version (`0` fresh; `old + 1` for a `replace` successor).

ReconciliationRunView.description: One reconciliation-run row, projected for the read. PII-free (ids + variance).

RecordDisputePhaseRequest.description:
The `POST /disputes/{dispute_id}/phases` request body: record one phase of a
chargeback dispute. `{dispute_id}` (the dispute's external id) comes from the
PATH; the target seller ledger is the body's own `tenant_id` (tenant in body,
not path — the vhp-core REST convention); the `(dispute, write)` PEP gate
authorizes it. The LEDGER chooses the variant at `opened` from `funds_at_open`
(`"withheld"` ⇒ cash-hold, `"not_moved"` ⇒ AR-reclass); `phase` is one of
`"opened" | "won" | "lost" | "partial"` (Group B implements `opened`).
`cycle` defaults to 1 and increments on a re-open. `invoice_id` is required
for an AR-reclass `opened` (the disputed `(payer, invoice)` grain), ignored
for cash-hold. `scale` is advisory; `effective_at` `None` ⇒ stamped at post
time.

disputed_amount_minor.description:
The disputed amount in minor units (`> 0`): the **gross** claim (what the
buyer paid / the bank reverses), NOT net of the PSP fee — the ledger sizes a
`CASH_HOLD` cash leg at `net = settled − fee` itself.

effective_at.description: Phase instant; `None` ⇒ stamped at post time (current-month period).

funds_at_open.description:
The funds-movement fact: `"withheld"` (card rails) | `"not_moved"`
(invoice/ACH) — read at `opened` to choose the variant.

invoice_id.description:
The disputed `(payer, invoice)` AR grain — required for an AR-reclass
`opened`, ignored for cash-hold.

scale.description: Advisory currency scale; the ledger resolves the authoritative one.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this disputes within; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

RecordDisputePhaseResponse.description:
The `POST /disputes/{dispute_id}/phases` response when the phase POSTED
inline: a reference to the dispute phase posting. A fresh phase renders `201`,
an idempotent replay `200` (the handler reads `replayed`).

owner.description: The owning gear: a string, since no CHECK holds the column to a set (P-D-217).

RefundQuarantinedResponse.description:
The `POST /refunds` response when the refund references a payment with no
resolvable origin settlement: the refund was durably QUARANTINED (HTTP 202
Accepted), NOT posted. `status` is the fixed `refund-quarantined` token; `flow`
+ `business_id` are the quarantine queue key and `quarantined_at` the intake
instant. No posting handle — nothing has posted (and de-quarantine re-validates
all §4.7 caps + the then-current D2 threshold + dispute state before any post).
Mirrors [`AllocationQueuedResponse`].

quarantined_at.description: When the intake durably quarantined the request.

status.description: Always `refund-quarantined` (a normal-body kebab-case token, not an error).

RefundRequest.description:
The `POST /refunds` request body: one PSP refund phase to record (the
**money-out** side that unwinds a settled receipt). The target seller ledger
is the body's own `tenant_id` (tenant in body, not path — the vhp-core REST
convention); the `(entry, post)` PEP gate authorizes it (a refund posts a
balanced journal entry into the seller's ledger, like the credit/debit notes,
design §8 / Phase-1 precedent). `pattern` selects the economic shape
(`"A_UNALLOCATED"` / `"B_RESTORE_AR"`); `phase` the lifecycle stage
(`"initiated"` / `"confirmed"` / `"rejected"` / `"voided"` /
`"unknown_final"`). `invoice_id` is required for Pattern B (the AR it
restores), absent for Pattern A. `two_stage` defaults to `true` (the
conservative `REFUND_CLEARING` shape). `relates_to_refund_id` + `direction`
drive a refund-of-refund (Group E); a first-order refund omits both (direction
defaults to outbound). `scale` is advisory; the ledger resolves the
authoritative currency scale.

amount_minor.description: The cash to return, in minor units (`> 0`).

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency (all legs share it; MUST match the origin settlement's).

direction.description:
The economic direction (refund-of-refund only): `OUTBOUND` | `CLAWBACK`.
`None` ⇒ `OUTBOUND` for a first-order refund (the domain default is
claw-back ONLY when a `relates_to_refund_id` is set; a first-order refund is
always outbound, so the DTO defaults to outbound here and lets
`validate_shape` require the link for an explicit claw-back).

invoice_id.description:
The invoice whose AR the refund restores — REQUIRED for Pattern B, MUST be
absent for Pattern A (validated by the domain `validate_shape`).

payer_tenant_id.description: The tenant the refund returns cash to (the original payer).

payment_id.description: The origin settled payment the refund unwinds (NOT NULL both patterns, D7).

psp_refund_id.description: The PSP's refund id — the idempotency grain together with `phase`.

refund_id.description:
The business id of this refund — the `refund` row's surrogate PK +
the `GET /refunds/{refundId}` handle (NOT the idempotency key).

relates_to_refund_id.description:
The prior refund this one references (refund-of-refund link); `None` for a
first-order refund.

scale.description: Advisory currency scale; the ledger resolves the authoritative one.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this posts into; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

two_stage.description:
`true` (default) ⇒ the two-stage `REFUND_CLEARING` shape; `false` ⇒ the
single-step shape (D1). `None` ⇒ `true`.

RefundResponse.description:
The `POST /refunds` (and the refund leg of `POST /refund-with-credit-note`)
response when the refund POSTED inline: a reference to the refund-stage
posting. A fresh stage renders `201`, an idempotent replay `200` (the handler
reads `replayed`). Mirrors [`SettlePaymentResponse`].

RefundView.description:
The `GET /refunds/{refundId}` response: the recorded refund + its clearing
state (Group G). Drawn from the `refund` row (the surrogate `(tenant,
refund_id)` grain). `clearing_state` is the two-stage `REFUND_CLEARING` drain
state (`PENDING` ⇒ stage-1 open / `SETTLED` ⇒ drained or single-step /
`REVERSED` ⇒ a PSP reject/void line-negated the stage-1). Tenant-scoped
(SQL-level BOLA): an unknown refund — or one outside the caller's subtree —
yields a `404` (no existence leak).

phase.description: The latest lifecycle phase recorded on this refund.

relates_to_refund_id.description: The refund-of-refund forward link (`None` for a first-order refund).

reverses_entry_id.description: The negated stage-1 entry id on a PSP reject/void (`None` otherwise).

RefundWithCreditNoteRequest.description:
The `POST /refund-with-credit-note` request body: post a refund AND its paired
S3 credit note ATOMICALLY in one transaction as two linked entries (K-3,
design §4.4). The refund carries the credit note's id (`credit_note_id`) so the
two are linked; AR is never overstated between them (both commit or neither).
The target seller ledger is the body's own `tenant_id`; the `(entry, post)` PEP
gate authorizes it. Carries BOTH the refund request and the credit-note request
inline (each its own idempotency grain) — a composite, not a discriminated
union.

credit_note.description: The paired S3 credit note to post atomically with the refund.

RefundWithCreditNoteResponse.description:
The `POST /refund-with-credit-note` response: references to BOTH posted entries
(the refund + the paired credit note), committed atomically. Always `201` on a
fresh composite (an idempotent replay of an already-posted composite renders
`200`; both halves replay together since they share the post txn).

credit_note_entry_id.description: The posted credit-note entry id (the paired second entry).

replayed.description: `true` ⇒ an idempotent replay of an already-posted composite (both halves).

RegisterEntitiesRequest.description: Request DTO for registering GTS entities.

entities.description: Array of GTS entities to register.

results.description: Results for each entity in the request.

RegisterResultDto.description: Result of registering a single entity.

oneOf.description: Successfully registered entity.
Failed to register entity.

gts_id.description: The GTS ID that was attempted, if available.

RegisterSummaryDto.description: Summary of a batch registration operation.

oneOf.description: Present when this candidate failed.

gts_id.description: A registration names only identifiers, so this is always the submitted one.

RegistrationKindDto.description: The discriminator of a registration operation.

status.description:
Progress only — the outcomes are on the items and are deliberately not
aggregated here.

ReidentifyRequestDto.description:
`POST …/audit/reidentify` request body: the payer to re-identify + the
machine `reason_code`. The free-text `reason` is the **`X-Investigation-Reason`
header** (§5), not a body field; both reason and `reason_code` are required
(a missing one is rejected `MISSING_INVESTIGATION_REASON`).

target_scope.description:
The tenant whose PII map to re-identify against (defaults to the caller's
own). A different tenant is the forensic cross-tenant path (§5):
authorized for `(entry, reidentify)` on the target, else
`CROSS_TENANT_ACCESS_DENIED`.

ReidentifyResponseDto.description:
`POST …/audit/reidentify` response: the recovered opaque `pii_ref` (the
pointer into the external PII store; never the PII itself).

ReleaseAssetDto.description: A downloadable file attached to a release.

assets.description: The release's downloadable files; `[]` when it has none.

clone_url.description:
Always present: falls back to the canonical github.com URL when the
row was mirrored before the column existed.

node_id.description: GitHub's GraphQL global id, as GitHub itself returns it.

RequestChildConversionDto.description:
Request body for `POST /tenants/{tenant_id}/child-conversions`
(initiator = parent acting on a direct child). Same field set as
[`RequestOwnConversionDto`] plus the explicit `child_tenant_id`
because the URL binds the parent — the converting child has to be
identified in the body.

comment.description:
Optional caller-supplied rationale. Same `1..=1000` chars
contract as [`RequestOwnConversionDto::comment`].

RequestOwnConversionDto.description:
Request body for
`POST /tenants/{tenant_id}/conversions` (initiator = converting
tenant). `target_mode` is REQUIRED — the service rejects any value
other than the strict binary inverse of the tenant's current
`self_managed` flag with `code=validation`. `comment` is optional
(1..=1000 chars when supplied; empty strings are a contract bug and
surface as `code=validation`).

comment.description:
Optional caller-supplied rationale. The service rejects
`Some("")` and any value over 1000 chars with
`code=validation` BEFORE the DB write. The `min_length` /
`max_length` constraints below advertise the same contract
to the served `OpenAPI` so codegen clients see the bound
statically rather than discovering it via a runtime 400.

reason.description: Operator / Finance reason (audit context; recorded with the actor).

ResolvedTenantMetadataDto.description:
Effective-value resolution result for the inheritance-aware walk-up
surface.

`resolved == false` carries no `value` — the terminal empty state
of an `OverrideOnly` schema, a `self_managed` barrier, or a walk
that reached the root without a hit. Distinct from
`metadata_entry_not_found` (which only fires on the single-entry
`GET` path); `resolve` always returns HTTP 200 per FEATURE §3.

id.description: Specific resource ID (for GET/UPDATE/DELETE on a single resource).

properties.description: Additional resource properties for policy evaluation.

ResourceRefDto.description:
Wire-projection of [`usage_collector_sdk::ResourceRef`]. Mirrors the SDK
shape verbatim; the SDK struct stays `utoipa`-free.

etag.description: The row's state tag, what a mutation of this pair must present.

set_by.description:
The administrator of a strict ancestor who recorded it: an
administrator's identity, masked for a caller not authorized for
unmasked PII.

tenant_id.description: The tenant restricted.

updated_at.description: When it was last changed, RFC 3339.

ResubmitRequest.description:
A resubmit body carrying the preparer's edited intent (the stored `intent`
jsonb shape). The kind cannot change; the approval returns to `PENDING`.

RetentionRuleBodyDto.description:
Retention rule body in requests and responses.

@cpt-cf-file-storage-fr-retention-policies

ReturnPaymentRequest.description:
The `POST /payments/{payment_id}/returns` request body: claw a settled
receipt back out (the reversal of a money-in). `{payment_id}` (the original
settled payment) comes from the PATH; `psp_return_id` is the idempotency key
(a re-post replays). `scale` is advisory; `effective_at` `None` ⇒ stamped at
post time.

effective_at.description: Return instant; `None` ⇒ stamped at post time (current-month period).

psp_return_id.description: External return identity — the idempotency key.

scale.description: Advisory currency scale; the ledger resolves the authoritative one.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this returns within; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

ReturnPaymentResponse.description:
The `POST /payments/{payment_id}/returns` response: a reference to the return
posting. A fresh return renders `201`, an idempotent replay `200` (the
handler reads `replayed`).

RevaluationRunRequest.description:
Trigger an unrealized (Mode-B) revaluation for one period across the monetary
scopes `{AR, UNALLOCATED, REUSABLE_CREDIT}` (design §4.5). `tenant_id` rides
the body (the vhp-core write convention). Each scope is idempotent on
`(tenant, period_id, scope)` — re-posting the same period replays the
already-posted scopes. A no-op when the tenant is Mode-A
(`revaluation_enabled = false`).

period_id.description:
The period to revalue (`YYYYMM`). Must be an OPEN period at run time (the
run posts INTO it); a CLOSED/absent period is rejected by the posting gate.

tenant_id.description: The seller tenant whose foreign-currency monetary positions are remeasured.

RevaluationRunResponse.description: The outcome of a revaluation run — one entry per monetary scope.

RevaluationScopeOutcomeDto.description:
One monetary scope's revaluation outcome (aggregated across its per-payer
entries — an entry spans only one payer, so a scope fans out over payers).

entries.description: Entries freshly written this call (a full idempotent replay reports `0`).

grains.description: Grains moved across those entries (a forward run only; `0` for a no-op).

status.description:
The outcome: `posted` (entries written), `nothing_to_post` (no
cross-currency movement / a full idempotent replay), or `disabled` (Mode A).

RevenueDisaggregationEntryDto.description:
One disaggregated recognized-revenue grain in the `GET
/revenue/disaggregation` response: the revenue RECOGNIZED into
`revenue_stream` during `period_id` (`Σ amount_minor` of the DONE recognition
segments at that grain), in minor units of `currency`. A row of
[`RevenueDisaggregationResponse::entries`].

currency.description: ISO currency of the recognized amount.

period_id.description: The fiscal period the revenue recognized in (`YYYYMM`).

recognized_minor.description: Revenue recognized into this `(period, stream)` grain, in minor units.

revenue_stream.description: The revenue stream the recognized revenue books to.

RevenueDisaggregationResponse.description:
The `GET /revenue/disaggregation` response: recognized ASC 606 revenue
disaggregated by `(period_id, revenue_stream)`, ordered by
`(period_id, revenue_stream)`. NOTE: like `ar-aging`, this is a **computed
aggregate report** (a grouped SUM over the recognized segments), not a
paginated row collection — it keeps plain `?tenant_id=&period_id=` query
params (no `OData` `$filter` / `Page` envelope).

ReversalRequestDto.description:
The `POST /journal-entries/{entryId}/reversals` request body. The reversed
entry is the `{entryId}` path id; the tenant is the caller's auth context.
The reversal lands in the supplied `period_id` (a still-OPEN period — it may
differ from the original's) effective `effective_at`; both default
server-side to the original's period / today when omitted.

effective_at.description: GL effective date of the reversal; `None` ⇒ today (UTC).

period_id.description: Target OPEN period for the reversal; `None` ⇒ the original's period.

reason.description: Audit reason for the reversal (recorded by the caller's actor).

line.description:
GitHub's current diff anchors, which its own UI positions inline
comments by; `position` above is the deprecated form.

original_position.description:
Line position at comment-creation time — the stable anchor across
later force-pushes.

position.description:
Line position in the current diff; absent once GitHub considers the
commented-on line outdated.

pull_request_review_id.description: The review this inline comment belongs to, as GitHub reports it.

ReviewThreadDto.description: A mirrored PR review conversation thread, served by the extended API.

ScheduleChangeResponse.description:
The `POST /recognition-schedules/{schedule_id}/changes` response: a small
reference to the change's outcome. `new_schedule_id` is the successor version's
id on a `replace` (`null` on a `cancel`); `status` is the original schedule's
resulting status (`"REPLACED"` | `"CANCELLED"`). Always `200` (the change is
applied or an idempotent replay).

new_schedule_id.description: The successor schedule version's id on a `replace`; `null` on a `cancel`.

schedule_id.description: The original schedule that was cancelled / replaced.

SearchCategoryDto.description:
The category a hit is filed under. Categories are flat, so this is the
whole breadcrumb.

key.description: The category slug, as carried in the setting key.

SearchHitDto.description:
One search result. A declaration-level hit carries no scope; an override
hit names the scope where the matched value is set.

category.description: The category the setting is filed under.

declaration_id.description: Identity of the declaration, for a follow-up read.

description.description: The declaration's description, when it has one.

mode.description:
`standard` or `advanced`, from the declaration. A tag for grouping,
never a filter — no hit is withheld by it.

scope.description:
The scope path where the matched override is set. Absent on a
declaration-level hit.

tenant_id.description: The tenant owning that scope. Absent on a declaration-level hit.

value.description:
The matched stored value — the override for a `value` hit, the Schema
Default for a `default_value` hit — masked by classification exactly
as a read would mask it. Absent for a hit on the key, description or
category name.

SecretMetadataDto.description: Access metadata returned alongside the secret value.

is_inherited.description: Whether the secret came from an ancestor tenant.

owner_tenant_id.description: The tenant that owns this secret.

sharing.description: The sharing mode that governed the lookup result.

type.description: Secret type as its full GTS type id.

version.description: Monotonic version of the resolved secret (also returned as `ETag`).

ServiceAccountCreateRequestDto.description:
Request body for
`POST /account-management/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/service-accounts`.
`tenant_id` comes from the path.

`name` / `scopes` are not secret, so `Debug` is plain-derived —
unlike [`ServiceAccountCredentialsDto`] below, which hand-writes a
redacting one.

name.description:
Short caller-chosen name, unique among the tenant's live
accounts. Adapters commonly derive the client id as
`svc-<tenant_id>-<name>`, but that format is a convention rather
than contract; the listing echoes this `name` back so callers
correlate without parsing client ids. AM bounds the length; the
charset and uniqueness are the provider's to enforce.

scopes.description:
Client scopes to attach; validated against the provider's
allowlist.

ServiceAccountCredentialsDto.description:
Live credentials returned by create and rotate-secret.

The secret is returned ONLY here — there is no read-back endpoint.
`Debug` is hand-written to redact it, and both handlers set
`Cache-Control: no-store` so no intermediary retains the body.

client_id.description:
The provider-assigned client id, used to address rotate-secret
and revoke. Opaque to callers.

client_secret.description:
The `client_credentials` secret. Persist it immediately;
recovery from loss is a rotate, not a read.

subject_id.description:
The account's subject id (`sub` of issued tokens) — use it for
RBAC bindings.

token_url.description: OAuth token endpoint for the `client_credentials` grant.

client_id.description:
The provider-assigned client id, used to address rotate-secret
and revoke.

enabled.description: Whether the client can currently authenticate.

name.description:
The caller-supplied `name` this account was created with,
reported verbatim by the provider. This is how a caller
correlates a name it submitted with an opaque `client_id` —
notably to reconcile a create that returned `409`
`AMBIGUOUS_OUTCOME`.

scopes.description:
Attached client scopes as reported by the `IdP` — includes
realm-default scopes, not only the requested ones.

ServiceAccountListDto.description:
Response body for
`GET /account-management/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/service-accounts`.

Deliberately not a `toolkit_odata::Page` like the user listing: the
contract is unpaginated (the provider returns the tenant's whole
collection), because this listing is also the reconciliation path for
an ambiguous create — "is my name already live here?" must not be a
multi-round-trip question with a cursor to invalidate.

service_accounts.description: The tenant's service accounts, in provider order.

SetDualControlPolicyRequest.description:
A new dual-control threshold policy version to write (DC8). `effective_from`
defaults to now when omitted; out-of-range D2/A6/TTL is rejected (409, no clamp).

SetFxRevaluationModeRequest.description:
A new FX revaluation-mode version to write (VHP-1986). `effective_from`
defaults to now when omitted. An unknown `revaluation_mode` is rejected (400),
never coerced.

effective_from.description: When this version takes effect; defaults to now.

revaluation_mode.description:
`MODE_A` (defer the period-end revaluation to the tenant's ERP — the
fail-safe default) or `MODE_B` (BSS is the ledger of record and runs the
unrealized revaluation).

scope_owner_id.description: Target owner id (required when `scope = "user"`; omit for tenant scope).

SetPostingPolicyRequest.description:
A new posting-policy version to write (VHP-1853). `effective_from` defaults to
now when omitted. An unknown `missing_mapping_mode`, or empty / non-positive /
non-monotone `ar_aging_thresholds`, is rejected (400), never coerced.

ar_aging_thresholds.description:
AR-aging bucket upper-bounds: strictly increasing positive day counts
(e.g. `[30, 60, 90]` → `current / 1-30 / 31-60 / 61-90 / 90+`).

effective_from.description: When this version takes effect; defaults to now.

missing_mapping_mode.description:
`SUSPENSE` (route unmapped items to suspense — the default) or `HARD_BLOCK`
(reject a post that carries an unmapped item).

SetReactionReq.description: Request DTO for setting a reaction.

change_set_id.description: The change set the write belongs to.

etag.description: The scope's new value state tag; the next write presents it.

masked.description: Whether the values carry the mask token.

new_value.description: The value after, masked by classification; absent after a removal.

old_value.description: The value before, masked by classification; absent when no row existed.

tenant_id.description: The target as a tenant id.

value.description:
The new value, validated against the declaration's value type. Kept as
text until the guards have seen it: a number is refused, not rounded.

SettingItemDto.description: One entry of the browse page: a key with its own outcome.

detail.description: What went wrong, for the failure outcomes.

oneOf.description: The effective value, when `outcome` is `resolved`.
The flagged override, when `outcome` is `needs_review`.

mode.description:
`standard` or `advanced`, from the declaration. Absent only for a
requested key that has no declaration. Mode is a tag, never a filter:
every page carries every setting and a client groups them itself.

SettlePaymentRequest.description:
The `POST /payments` request body: a settled payment to record (the
**money-in** side). The target seller ledger is the body's own `tenant_id`
(tenant in body, not path — the vhp-core REST convention); the `(payment,
write)` PEP gate authorizes it. `scale` is the payment's currency scale as
known to the caller — advisory; the ledger resolves the authoritative
per-line scale from the provisioned currency config. `effective_at` `None`
⇒ the receipt is stamped at post time.

effective_at.description: Receipt instant; `None` ⇒ stamped at post time (current-month period).

fee_minor.description: Processor's withheld cut in minor units (`<= gross`).

gross_minor.description: Gross received in minor units (what the payer was charged).

payment_id.description: External payment identity — the idempotency key (a re-settle replays).

scale.description: Advisory currency scale; the ledger resolves the authoritative one.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this settles into; the PEP gate target.
Carried in the body, not the path.

SettlePaymentResponse.description:
The `POST /payments` response: a reference to the settlement posting. A
fresh settle renders `201`, an idempotent replay `200` (the handler reads
`replayed`).

SettlementView.description:
The `GET /payments/{payment_id}/settlement` response: the per-payment money-out
serialization counters (read-surface R4). Drawn from the `payment_settlement`
row (the `(tenant, payment_id)` grain) — the settled / fee / allocated /
refunded / clawed-back running totals the money-out caps serialize against.
The persisted `version` (the optimistic-concurrency counter) is INTERNAL and
not surfaced. Tenant-scoped (SQL-level BOLA): a payment that was never settled
— or one outside the caller's subtree — yields a `404` (no existence leak).
Mirrors [`RefundView`].

allocated_minor.description: The portion of the pool already drained to open AR (money-out).

clawed_back_minor.description: The portion clawed back (a refund-of-refund / PSP claw-back).

fee_minor.description: The PSP fee withheld from the settled receipt.

refunded_minor.description: The portion already returned to the payer via refunds.

refunded_unallocated_minor.description: The portion refunded from the still-unallocated pool (Pattern A).

settled_minor.description: The gross settled amount recorded for the payment (money-in).

SharingModeDto.description: Sharing mode for the REST transport layer.

SizeLimitsDto.description: Size limits in a policy body.

max_bytes.description: Global maximum file size in bytes (`null` = unlimited at this level).

oneOf.description:
Pricing's usage of the SKU through the port pricing fills (P-D-197); `null` when no port is
registered, when it refuses the caller, or when it cannot answer.

note.description:
The submitter's reason: at most 2000 characters (400 `NOTE_TOO_LONG`), stored on the unit
as `submit_note` and on the submit's history row, as sent (P-D-213, P-D-219).

SkuDto.description: Wire representation of the registry Sku.

archived_at.description:
When the retired SKU was archived (P-D-263); null while it is not. The SKU list hides it
unless asked `archived eq true`; a read by id ignores the mark. Not a lifecycle.

archived_by.description: Who archived it; null while it is not archived.

archived_by_name.description:
The current name of `archived_by` (P-D-262), as `created_by_name` names its actor; null
when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

created_by_name.description:
The current name of `created_by` (P-D-262): its display name, else first and last name, else
username, from Account Management under the caller's rights; "System" for a system actor.
Null when no name is available now, and on a write answer.

oneOf.description: A dated lifecycle change that has not arrived (P-D-249). Null when none is pending.

retire_pending.description: Set while a retire is in review (P-D-248). The lifecycle stays.

SkuListItem.description:
One item of the SKU list: the SKU's fields and pricing's `usage` (P-D-197), `null` when the
port is absent, refuses or cannot answer.

category_id.description: Omitted keeps the category, `null` clears it (P-D-196), a value sets it.
Optional (P-D-196): omitted or `null` stays null, with no fallback to the default category.

SkuRow.description: Compatibility projection consumed by the unchanged REST row parser.

SkuUsageDto.description:
Pricing's usage of a SKU (P-D-197): its price-book entries, the distinct currencies of their
books (sorted), their prices by state, and the distinct plans naming them. Information for the
SKUs screen; never a fence input.

SkuUsagePricesDto.description: A SKU's prices by state, as pricing counts them (pricing D-428).

StageSecretRequest.description:
`POST /settings/{key}/secret-stage`: the plaintext to stage ahead of the
step-up redirect.

value.description:
The secret value, validated against the declaration's type exactly as
a set validates it.

request_id.description: Idempotency key: any UUID; generated by the server when omitted.

oneOf.description: Web search configuration.

StreamStartedData.description:
Stream header event carrying the stream request ID and server-generated
assistant message ID.

Emitted as the first event in every SSE stream (both new generations and
replays). `is_new_turn` distinguishes replayed completed turns from live
generations.

is_new_turn.description:
`true` for a live generation (new turn); `false` when the stream
replays an already-completed turn (idempotent replay).

oneOf.description:
Present when a thread summary is included in the context window.
UI can display an informational indicator.

Subject.description: The authenticated subject making the request.

properties.description:
Additional subject properties for policy evaluation.
The subject's home tenant ID goes here as `"tenant_id"`.

type.description:
Subject type (e.g., "user", "service").
Serialized as `"type"` to match the `AuthZEN` spec.

SubmitEntitiesRequest.description:
A submission of one or more entities.

`items` and not `entities`: the operation result, the discovery page and
`Page<T>` all call their array `items`, so this is the house word for "the
array in this envelope". It is also the name v1 does *not* use, which keeps
the T24a promotion a loud break rather than one that turns on the element
shape.

dry_run.description:
Predict the batch using one snapshot and an overlay of prior candidates' effects.
Record outcomes without entity-state writes or reservations.

Defaults to `false`; participates in the idempotency fingerprint.

SubmitEntityDto.description:
One entity in a submission.

`SubmitEntityDto` and not `SubmitCandidateDto`: "candidate" is the domain's
word for a submitted-but-not-yet-admitted entity, and this type is the wire
form, whose name reaches callers as an `OpenAPI` component.

expected_resource_version.description:
Optimistic precondition. **Omit** to require that the identifier does not
exist; a literal `0` is refused. A positive version names a content
revision: the entity must exist at exactly that `resource_version`, and a
mismatch fails the candidate terminally rather than rebasing it.

Optional positive precondition; acceptance rejects zero and negatives.

force.description:
ADR-0004: waive one cross-minor check when the deployment permits it.
Intra-entity revisions are never waivable. The revision records the
effective waiver as `compat_forced`.

gts_id.description:
The canonical GTS identifier. A non-canonical spelling is refused rather
than normalized.

SyncSummaryDto.description: Result of one sync pass, as served by the extended sync endpoint.

stale_rows_deleted.description: Rows hard-deleted because a complete listing no longer contained them.

fetched_at_secs.description: When this capability was last fetched (Unix timestamp in seconds)

TamperStatusDto.description:
The tamper-status of a resolved scope, the `GET …/audit/tamper-status`
response: `scope_frozen` (any ACTIVE freeze), the freeze rows, and a derived
`verified` (= `!scope_frozen`, the MVP derivation — see
[`crate::infra::audit::retrieval::AuditRetrievalReader::tamper_status_in_txn`]).

Wire-shape enum for `target_mode` on every conversion-request
surface. Mirrors [`TargetMode`] one-to-one. Defined locally for the
same `OpenAPI`-enum-preservation reason as the other wire enums.

TaxBreakdownDto.description: One tax component of an invoice to post, already computed by the tax engine.

TenantAncestorDto.description:
One node on the path from the listing's `tenant_id` down to a
recursively listed descendant
(`GET /tenants/{tenant_id}/children?recursive=true`).

tenant_type.description:
Chained GTS tenant-type identifier; omitted on a transient
types-registry blip (same policy as `TenantDto.tenant_type`).
Absent or a string, never `null` — the schema says so.

root_id.description: The context tenant ID (tenant being operated on).

TenantCreateRequestDto.description:
Request body for `POST /tenants`.

Mirrors `TenantCreateRequest` in the `OpenAPI` spec. `name`,
`parent_id`, and `tenant_type` (chained GTS identifier) are
required; `self_managed` defaults to `false` and
`provisioning_metadata` is an opaque payload forwarded to the
`IdP` plugin. The new child's UUID is **not** part of the request
— AM allocates it server-side so two parallel clients cannot
collide on the same id.

provisioning_metadata.description:
Opaque provider-specific provisioning context forwarded to the
`IdP` plugin. Typed as a JSON object (not `Value`) so the wire
contract — yaml `type: [object, 'null']` — is enforced by serde
at the boundary: arrays / scalars are rejected with a clean
400 before the request ever touches the service or the plugin.

TenantDto.description:
AM-internal projection. Wider than `tenant_resolver_sdk::TenantInfo` for
admin/UI consumers (carries lifecycle timestamps + depth).

Internal columns (raw `tenant_type_uuid`, retention/claim columns) never
cross this boundary. `tenant_type: None` only on a transient registry
blip — reads do not block on it.

ancestors.description:
Ancestor chain relative to the listing's `tenant_id`, ordered
from the child of `tenant_id` down to this tenant's direct
parent; empty for a direct child. Present only on
`GET /tenants/{tenant_id}/children?recursive=true` -- omitted
from every other response (the key is absent, not `null`).

child_count.description:
Number of **direct** children visible to the caller, resolved at
read time: scope-filtered (children behind a self-managed barrier
the caller cannot penetrate are not counted), excludes
AM-internal `provisioning` rows, includes soft-`deleted`
children. `0` for a leaf. Derived field (not a stored column) —
not available in `$filter` / `$orderby`.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-delete tombstone. `Some(_)` exactly when `status == deleted`;
omitted on the wire otherwise. Mirrors the SDK / storage column
`Tenant.deleted_at`; the retention sweep becomes eligible at
`deleted_at + retention_window` and is owned by the reaper.

TenantMetadataEntryDto.description:
One metadata entry. `tenant_id` is echoed from the path so consumers carry
the full `(tenant_id, type_id)` identity tuple; the SDK projection drops
`tenant_id` by design.

TenantStatus.description:
Tenant lifecycle status.

Mirrors the SMALLINT encoding stored in `tenants.status` and
`tenant_closure.descendant_status` (the canonical mapping is
`Active = 1`, `Suspended = 2`, `Deleted = 3`). Use [`as_smallint`] /
[`from_smallint`] to cross the DB boundary so the mapping stays in
one place — duplicating it elsewhere risks future drift.

[`as_smallint`]: TenantStatus::as_smallint
[`from_smallint`]: TenantStatus::from_smallint

TenantStatusDto.description:
Wire-shape enum for `Tenant.status` on the REST surface.

Mirrors the SDK-visible variants of
[`account_management_sdk::TenantStatus`] one-to-one (the
AM-internal `provisioning` variant is never surfaced). Defined
locally rather than reusing the SDK enum because the upstream
type lives in `tenant-resolver-sdk` without a `utoipa::ToSchema`
derive — surfacing the SDK enum verbatim through
`#[schema(value_type = String)]` would erase the enum constraint
from the served `OpenAPI`, leaving codegen clients with `String`
instead of `active | suspended | deleted`.

TenantUpdateRequestDto.description:
PATCH body for `/tenants/{tenant_id}`. Only `name` is mutable; status
transitions go through `/suspend`, `/unsuspend`, `DELETE`. Empty patch →
service returns `code=validation`. `deny_unknown_fields` keeps the wire
envelope locked.

TextSpan.description: A character span within response text.

ThreadSummaryInfo.description:
Metadata about a thread summary applied to the current turn's context.

Sent in the `stream_started` event when the conversation has an active
thread summary. The UI can use this to show an informational banner.

token_estimate.description: Estimated token cost of the summary in the context window.

ToolPhase.description: Lifecycle phase of a tool invocation within a stream.

One scope on the inheritance trail, with the setter identity and
timestamp the administrative read is allowed to show.

set_by.description:
Who set the row here: an administrator's identity, masked for a
caller not authorized for unmasked PII.

tenant_id.description: The tenant inspected.

Request to transfer ownership of a file (`POST /files/{id}/transfer`).

@cpt-cf-file-storage-fr-ownership-transfer

TriggerRecognitionRunRequest.description:
The `POST /recognition-runs` request body: trigger an ASC 606 recognition
run for one fiscal period (release the period's due `PENDING` segments). The
target seller ledger is the body's own `tenant_id` (tenant in body, not path
— the vhp-core REST convention); the `(entry, post)` PEP gate authorizes it
(a run posts `DR CL / CR Revenue` journal entries). `run_id` is the
run-trigger idempotency key: `None` ⇒ the ledger mints a fresh one (a first,
un-keyed trigger); a stable one makes retries idempotent (a replay returns
the prior run reference without starting a second run).

period_id.description: The fiscal period to release due segments for (`YYYYMM`).

run_id.description: The run-trigger idempotency key; `None` ⇒ the ledger mints a fresh one.

tenant_id.description:
The seller tenant whose ledger this releases revenue in; the PEP gate
target. Carried in the body, not the path.

`POST /ledger/reconciliation-runs` request body: the period + the named check
to run for the caller's own tenant.

run_id.description: The server-minted reconciliation-run id (the `GET …/{run_id}` key tail).

TurnStatusState.description: Turn state as reported by the turn status endpoint.
